a12.speaker: Kirsty Coventry, IOC President-elect
a12.name: Kirsty Coventry
a12.title: IOC President-elect
a12.speech: "Next year, when we host the Youth Olympic Games, you are going to show the world what it is to be African, to feel African and to have that experience. You are ambassadors for the young generation of what the sporting movement can be, and the legacy the Youth Olympic Games can leave behind."

a12.speaker: Humphrey Kayange, Chair of the Dakar 2026 Coordination Commission
a12.name: Humphrey Kayange
a12.title: Chair of the Dakar 2026 Coordination Commission
a12.speech: "On behalf of the entire Commission, we're truly excited and looking forward to engaging with you. We're confident in your ability to deliver. Together, we will bring these Games to life and celebrate the Youth Olympic Games in a uniquely African way. I wish you all the best as you begin working across different functional areas in the coming weeks. We're looking forward to your success and the success of the Games."

a12.speaker: Ibrahima Wade, General Coordinator of the YOGOC
a12.name: Ibrahima Wade
a12.title: General Coordinator of the YOGOC
a12.speech: "At the Dakar 2026 Learning Academy, participants will receive appropriate support through tailored training modules and an environment where sport and Olympism will contribute to their professional development, based around the values of friendship, excellence and respect. These young recruits will go on to play an active role in delivering the first Youth Olympic Games in Africa."

a178.speaker: Jacquiline Amongin, Ugandan lawmaker (EALA member)
a178.name: Jacquiline Amongin
a178.title: Ugandan lawmaker (EALA member)
a178.speech: "The Assembly will not proceed with scrutiny or approval of the new budget until the Council provides the necessary funds to implement outstanding programs, including those of EALA's committees and plenary sessions," Amongin said.

a178.speaker: East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) (resolution)
a178.name: East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) (resolution)
a178.speech: The Assembly's decision cites the Council's failure to finance statutory activities, which lawmakers argue undermines the legislative process. The resolution also urges the EALA Speaker to consider extending the budget review period under Section 12 of the EAC Budget Act, 2009, if the situation remains unresolved.

a178.speaker: EALA lawmakers
a178.name: EALA lawmakers
a178.speech: Lawmakers emphasized that proper funding is essential to ensure institutional operations, oversight, and the passage of community laws critical to the integration process.

a528.speaker: Save the Children
a528.name: Save the Children
a528.speech: Said it would be forced to close 121 nutrition centres, including all of its centres in the southern city of Baidoa, one of the country's most vulnerable regions, as international aid cuts force the closure of more than a quarter of its health and nutrition facilities across Somalia.

a528.speaker: Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit
a528.name: Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit
a528.speech: According to the Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Unit, 1.8 million children in Somalia are projected to suffer from acute malnutrition this year, of whom an estimated 479,000 will suffer from severe acute malnutrition.

a528.speaker: Fatima, 25-year-old mother living in a displacement camp in Baidoa
a528.name: Fatima
a528.title: 25-year-old mother living in a displacement camp in Baidoa
a528.speech: Said Save the Children's nutrition programme saved her one-year-old daughter Fardowso, who was diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition and treated with high-nutrient food and medicine ; "If we were not able to get medicines and nutrition support here, we would have no other option but to see our children dying in front of us. There is no other service here so we would only see our children get progressively worse."

a528.speaker: Dr. Mustafa Mohammed, doctor at a Save the Children-supported stabilisation centre in Baidoa
a528.name: Dr. Mustafa Mohammed
a528.title: doctor at a Save the Children-supported stabilisation centre in Baidoa
a528.speech: "If our centre closes, children such as these will be put into grave danger. There is nowhere else for these children to go."

a528.speaker: Save the Children (aid agency)
a528.name: Save the Children (aid agency)
a528.speech: Says clinics are already overwhelmed, and by the end of the current rainy season in June - when hunger and malnutrition typically rise - conditions are expected to worsen ; called the funding gap a "political choice" with potentially deadly consequences.

a528.speaker: Hassan (Save the Children)
a528.name: Hassan (Save the Children)
a528.speech: Warned: "Unless funding is found, I fear that we will see deadly consequences for children."

a529.speaker: Office of the Vice President and Chairperson of the Economic Cluster (South Sudan)
a529.name: Office of the Vice President and Chairperson of the Economic Cluster (South Sudan)
a529.speech: According to the Office of the Vice President and Chairperson of Economic Cluster, the budget, presented by Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Marial Dongrin Ater, aims to accelerate economic recovery, ensure macroeconomic stability, and support the country's democratic process.

a529.speaker: Initial reports (unattributed press reports on Kenya's budget)
a529.name: Initial reports (unattributed press reports on Kenya's budget)
a529.speech: Initial reports indicate the military emerged as the biggest winner in the parliamentary reorganization of the Treasury's budget, while public financial management, education, and sports faced cuts.

a623.speaker: Hannington Gondwe, CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce
a623.name: Hannington Gondwe
a623.title: CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce
a623.speech: Argues that Malawi is at a critical economic crossroads as donor fatigue and shifting international aid policies threaten the country's financial stability, and that with the United States freezing key development funds and global financial institutions tightening their aid criteria, Malawi must urgently adopt new strategies to ensure sustainable growth and reduce its reliance on external funding ; notes that over 13% of Malawi's national budget - equivalent to $350 million - came from U.S. aid alone, that the freeze on USAID funds has affected healthcare, education and infrastructure, that 55% of Malawi's healthcare budget was previously covered by donor funding and the suspension has already led to medication shortages and disruption of HIV prevention programmes.

a623.speaker: Hannington Gondwe, CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce
a623.name: Hannington Gondwe
a623.title: CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce
a623.speech: Recommends that to counteract these economic challenges and create long-term financial resilience, Malawi must shift towards a digital economy ecosystem and invest in supporting infrastructure, including investing in digital infrastructure, promoting more e-government services and supporting tech startups and innovation hubs ; says Malawi should attract more public-private partnerships, expand renewable energy investments and modernise transport and logistics, and must prioritise economic diversification by expanding manufacturing and industrialisation, encouraging local and foreign investment and leveraging the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) ; concludes that the government, private sector and international partners must collaborate to ensure sustainable economic growth beyond aid dependency, and that "The time for action is now."

a643.speaker: The alleged Vavi affidavit / ‘spy report’
a643.name: The alleged Vavi affidavit / ‘spy report’
a643.speech: asserts that Constitutional Court justices are in the pay of the NED, with secret payments made to off-shore accounts in the Cayman Islands; that a Rwandan general is setting up secret military bases in South Africa and recruiting a mercenary army from South Africa, Botswana, Mozambique and Zimbabwe as a joint operation between Africans and the US, with the NED helping fund the covert project; that Zwelinzima Vavi was supposed to become a member of an Agang advisory board which the NED would fund to the tune of R500-million; that the NED secretly worked with the legal team that prosecuted Jacob Zuma; and that the organization was involved in Marikana, service delivery protests and xenophobic violence.

a643.speaker: Ronald Reagan, US President (1982 speech to the British Parliament)
a643.name: Ronald Reagan
a643.title: US President (1982 speech to the British Parliament)
a643.speech: proposed an institution “to foster the infrastructure of democracy – the system of a free press, unions, political parties, universities – which allows a people to choose their own way, to develop their own culture, to reconcile their own differences through peaceful means.”

a643.speaker: National Endowment for Democracy (NED) website / mission statement
a643.name: National Endowment for Democracy (NED) website / mission statement
a643.speech: describes its current mission: “Since its founding in 1983, the Endowment has remained on the leading edge of democratic struggles everywhere, while evolving into a multifaceted institution that is a hub of activity, resources and intellectual exchange for activists, practitioners and scholars of democracy the world over…. [The] NED is dedicated to fostering the growth of a wide range of democratic institutions abroad, including political parties, trade unions, free markets and business organizations, as well as the many elements of a vibrant civil society that ensure human rights, an independent media, and the rule of law.” ; has explained that the grant and training support it supplies “sends an important message of solidarity to many democrats who are working for freedom and human rights, often in obscurity and isolation. The Endowment is guided by the belief that freedom is a universal human aspiration that can be realized through the development of democratic institutions, procedures, and values. Democracy cannot be achieved through a single election and need not be based upon the model of the United States or any other particular country. Rather, it evolves according to the needs and traditions of diverse political cultures. By supporting this process, the Endowment helps strengthen the bond between indigenous democratic movements abroad and the people of the United States – a bond based on a common commitment to representative government and freedom as a way of life.”

a643.speaker: NED authorizing legislation (US Congress)
a643.name: NED authorizing legislation (US Congress)
a643.speech: was explicit about its non-governmental status, stating, “Nothing in this title shall be construed to make the Endowment an agency or establishment of the United States Government.”

a643.speaker: NED website (grants database)
a643.name: NED website (grants database)
a643.speech: According to the organization’s website, there are two current grants dealing with South Africa: one via the International Republican Institute for $100,000 “[t]o promote a pluralist public dialogue on policy solutions for issues facing South Africa on the national, provincial and local levels, as well as to foster demand for improved democratic governance on the local level through the efforts of the South African Institute of Race Relations (SAIRR),” and a second through the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs in the amount of $380,000 in which the “NDI seeks to strengthen parties’ awareness of strategies to increase women’s participation and promote dialogue about women’s service delivery needs.”

a643.speaker: A recent review (of the NED)
a643.name: A recent review (of the NED)
a643.speech: noted that the NED now raises about $0.65 from non-government sources for each $1.00 it receives from its annual Congressional appropriation.

a643.speaker: Critics on the left and the international human rights community
a643.name: Critics on the left and the international human rights community
a643.speech: have criticised NED programs on the grounds the NED focused too much on the mechanics of “free and fair elections” rather than a larger, more systemic civil rights/human rights culture.

a643.speaker: Analysts following NED activities
a643.name: Analysts following NED activities
a643.speech: say the institution’s growing emphasis on support for long-term democratic development, the building of civil society and funding of indigenous human rights groups has swayed most of those earlier critics towards more favourable views.

a643.speaker: Critics on the political right
a643.name: Critics on the political right
a643.speech: have taken heat at NED for the contention that they promote a “social democratic” agenda, based on its labour union relationships rather than a broader liberal catalogue of ideas.

a643.speaker: Freedom House (website and official history)
a643.name: Freedom House (website and official history)
a643.speech: says its key missions include “speaking out against the main threats to democracy and empower[ing] citizens to exercise their fundamental rights. We analyse the challenges to freedom; advocate for greater political and civil liberties; and support frontline activists to defend human rights and promote democratic change.” ; “We support non-violent civic initiatives in societies where freedom is denied or under threat and promote the right of all people to be free” and that it “acts as a catalyst for freedom through a combination of analysis, advocacy, and action. … Leading experts on democracy have called our flagship publication, Freedom in the World, an ‘essential source’ and ‘indispensable guide’ to democracy’s development.” ; “It was also among the earliest supporters of Poland's Solidarity trade union. Responding to growing strife in Africa, Freedom House sent study missions to Zimbabwe and South Africa led by Bayard Rustin. It also sent missions to assess conditions in Central America during the 1980s, as part of an on-going project to support centrist democratic forces, under siege from the Marxist left and the death squad right.” ; “Freedom House assisted these post-Communist societies in the establishment of independent media, independent think tanks, and the core institutions of electoral politics,” and “From South Africa to Tunisia, Kyrgyzstan to Indonesia, Freedom House has partnered with regional activists in bolstering civil society; worked to support women’s rights; sought justice for victims of torture; defended journalists and free expression advocates; and assisted those struggling to promote human rights in challenging political environments.”

a643.speaker: American Embassy spokesman (South Africa)
a643.name: American Embassy spokesman (South Africa)
a643.speech: told us, “The allegations against the US Government in the #vavireport are groundless and outrageous. The US has a strong record of supporting civil society, but we do not fund political parties or those who urge violence. NED is a non-profit independent from us. The US Congress and others fund them. They speak for themselves @nedemocracy.”

a643.speaker: A prominent younger African businessman (friend of the writer, anonymous)
a643.name: A prominent younger African businessman (friend of the writer
a643.title: anonymous)
a643.speech: “It’s incredible, the reports. There is a long claim that the US or CIA didn’t want Zuma to be president, it feeds into this, so it maybe perceived as reality. Almost all politicians hedge their risk especially when they are in trouble so Vavi is no exception. I think people who dissent are eliminated literally or figuratively speaking. I also think the government institutions are used to fight political battles – it’s the only game we know in this country and a legacy of the NP. The real key question, when all is said and done, is what will the ANC do if they were to lose an election?” ; “the propaganda reports are still juvenile and lack sophistication – a clear display of the lack of quality of our conspirators and leaders.”

a840.speaker: Salayea Magisterial Court (court record)
a840.name: Salayea Magisterial Court (court record)
a840.speech: Dismissed the case because the miners had a valid license, and advised the Ministry of Mines and Energy and the Forestry Development Authority (FDA) to settle the matter administratively.

a840.speaker: Global Forest Watch, an online platform that monitors forests worldwide (data)
a840.name: Global Forest Watch
a840.title: an online platform that monitors forests worldwide (data)
a840.speech: According to it, from 2002, Liberia lost 347,000 hectares of primary forest, with 20,000 hectares in Lofa County last year alone.

a840.speaker: Yassah Mulbah, chief officer of the Salayea Community Forest
a840.name: Yassah Mulbah
a840.title: chief officer of the Salayea Community Forest
a840.speech: "What is happening in the community is bad because they are damaging the forest that we are fighting to protect for our children and the future generation" ; "We are not happy because they are still destroying our forests, cutting down trees, and spoiling rivers and creeks because of gold-digging business."

a840.speaker: World Bank (data)
a840.name: World Bank (data)
a840.speech: According to it, last year mining contributed $665.4 million to Liberia's GDP and was a primary driver of economic growth along with construction; continued growth of 5.3 percent is projected for 2024 and an average of 5.6 percent between 2024 and 2025, spurred by mining and structural reforms.

a840.speaker: 16th Judicial Circuit Court in Bopolu (court record)
a840.name: 16th Judicial Circuit Court in Bopolu (court record)
a840.speech: Found the Turkish-owned company Bea Mountain liable and ordered it to pay over US$1.3 million in special damages and an additional US$3 million in general damages.

a840.speaker: Korninga B Community Forest locals (lawsuit)
a840.name: Korninga B Community Forest locals (lawsuit)
a840.speech: Sued Bea Mountain company for unauthorized entry into the community forest, accusing the company of cutting and destroying 2,800 logs while exploring for gold.

a840.speaker: Bondi Mandingo Authorized Community Forest, Gbarpolu (lawsuit)
a840.name: Bondi Mandingo Authorized Community Forest
a840.title: Gbarpolu (lawsuit)
a840.speech: Filed a $500,000 lawsuit against Harming Mining Group of Companies, accusing the company of cutting trees, digging large pits polluting water sources and establishing a camp protected by armed police.

a840.speaker: USAID report (2018)
a840.name: USAID report (2018)
a840.speech: Established that the Ministry of Mines weakened local forest management by authorizing mining in community forests without consulting local people and the FDA.

a840.speaker: Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL) report (2021)
a840.name: Center for Transparency and Accountability in Liberia (CENTAL) report (2021)
a840.speech: Highlighted weak coordination between the government offices in awarding semi-industrial-scale and small-scale mining licenses ; Found no redress mechanism for dissatisfied townspeople, except the courts, and that citizens' participation in mining was low.

a840.speaker: Dayugar Johnson, lead campaigner at Civil Society Independent Forest Monitors
a840.name: Dayugar Johnson
a840.title: lead campaigner at Civil Society Independent Forest Monitors
a840.speech: "In some areas, the FDA and Ministry of Mines and Energy lack the resources or capacity to enforce rules effectively" ; "This leaves community forests and... protected areas vulnerable to unauthorized mining activities..." ; Thinks corruption, high demands for minerals, limited awareness of the law and lack of alternative livelihood are a part of the problem.

a840.speaker: Rexford Sartuh, then-Assistant Minister for Exploration, Ministry of Mines and Energy
a840.name: Rexford Sartuh
a840.title: then-Assistant Minister for Exploration, Ministry of Mines and Energy
a840.speech: In a 2020 interview, disclosed that the Ministry of Mines did not recognize community forests. "They have their right to their land but when it comes to the issuance of mineral rights in Liberia, we don't consider them. They believe that we should ask them before we issue [licenses]. We should not," Sartuh said.

a840.speaker: Wilmot Paye, Minister of Mines and Energy
a840.name: Wilmot Paye
a840.title: Minister of Mines and Energy
a840.speech: In a WhatsApp chat with The DayLight, suggested that the mining law was superior to forestry laws and regulations. "Your query should further focus on what the Minerals and Mining Law of 2000 says," Paye texted, and did not say anything else.

a840.speaker: Drafters of a new mining law (draft seen by The DayLight)
a840.name: Drafters of a new mining law (draft seen by The DayLight)
a840.speech: Are proposing full recognition of all forestry and land laws and regulations.

a840.speaker: Mike Doryen, former FDA Managing Director
a840.name: Mike Doryen
a840.title: former FDA Managing Director
a840.speech: Criticized the Solway deal in 2020: "We are disappointed in the way the Ministry of Mines and Energy handled things. We think it has the propensity of discouraging our donors from making any more investments in the conservation area of our country."

a840.speaker: Yassah Mulbah, chief officer of the Salayea Community Forest
a840.name: Yassah Mulbah
a840.title: chief officer of the Salayea Community Forest
a840.speech: Says the FDA pledges to support Salayea ; "The community is frustrated, and people want to protest, but we urge patience as we seek help to protect our forest" ; "We are not satisfied because the government authorized us to manage our forest and resources."

a895.speaker: Bars and Night Club Owners Association of Zambia
a895.name: Bars and Night Club Owners Association of Zambia
a895.speech: Has expressed concern over the slow enforcement of the National Alcohol Policy ; warned that the continued rise in illicit alcohol production and sales is fuelling substance abuse, particularly among the youth ; “Enforce National Alcohol Policy to the latter”

a1024.speaker: Jeremiah Matthew Piah, Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.name: Jeremiah Matthew Piah
a1024.title: Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.speech: Describes construction of structures in wetlands across Montserrado County a "total mess," stating that such actions directly violate the Environmental Protection and Management Law of the Republic of Liberia ; "Before anyone builds in wetlands, they must comply with Liberia's zoning laws" ; emphasizes that no one should construct in wetlands or alleys, as these are protected areas ; "Now that we're taking steps to address the problem, some people are being hesitant" ; "We have a leader committed to changing the narrative and bringing development to Liberia. In this process, no one is untouchable."

a1024.speaker: Jeremiah Matthew Piah, Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.name: Jeremiah Matthew Piah
a1024.title: Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.speech: Discloses that the National Culture Center, where the RLJ hotel complex now stands, was demolished by the government and 52 acres of land were secured to build a new cultural center, but notes that land has been heavily encroached upon by squatters, leaving only 11 acres.

a1024.speaker: Jeremiah Matthew Piah, Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.name: Jeremiah Matthew Piah
a1024.title: Liberia's Minister of Information, Culture Affairs & Tourism
a1024.speech: Says government does not need to be "ready to develop the wetlands" before evicting illegal occupants: "Building in these areas is wrong, so we will remove the structures and develop the land when resources become available."

a1024.speaker: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a1024.name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a1024.speech: Warns that failure to comply with environmental regulations will lead to enforcement actions, including demolitions, fines, and potential legal prosecution; highlights the crucial role wetlands play in Liberia's climate resilience and disaster risk reduction, especially in preserving biodiversity and preventing natural disasters; and reaffirms its commitment to protecting the environment and ensuring all Liberians enjoy a clean and ecologically balanced environment.

a1024.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a1024.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1024.title: President of Liberia
a1024.speech: Emphasized the urgency of the initiative, warning that the continued destruction of wetlands, waterways, and beachfronts threatens both the environment and the livelihoods of community residents.

a1041.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1041.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a1041.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1041.speech: expressed his satisfaction with the Hawassa Industrial Park's new solar panel production facility, and recalled that the project stemmed from a prior agreement made during his visit to the Vietnamese Toyo solar panel factory and a meeting with the company's president.

a1041.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1041.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a1041.title: Ethiopian Prime Minister
a1041.speech: noted that two more solar panel factories are currently under construction, and praised the initiative, stating that it aligns with the nation's investment strategy to focus on value-added, “game-changing projects” that support Ethiopia's long-term economic goals.

a1041.speaker: Officials
a1041.name: Officials
a1041.speech: anticipate the output will significantly boost the country's manufacturing exports.

a1112.speaker: Larry André, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a1112.name: Larry André
a1112.title: United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a1112.speech: Took the opportunity to congratulate the minister on his recent appointment to head the ministerial department and wished him a fruitful term. He also expressed his satisfaction at the excellence of diplomatic relations between the United States of America and the Republic of Djibouti. Ambassador Larry André confirmed to the Minister of Labour the strengthening of cooperation on the national employment programme, particularly on youth employability, through USAID.

a1112.speaker: Isman Ibrahim Robleh, Djiboutian Minister of Labour, in charge of Administrative Reform
a1112.name: Isman Ibrahim Robleh
a1112.title: Djiboutian Minister of Labour, in charge of Administrative Reform
a1112.speech: For his part, assured him of his commitment to promoting collaboration between his ministerial department and USAID. He stressed the importance of removing obstacles to activities concerning the issue of youth employability in order to contribute to the country's development.

a1460.speaker: Daud Aweis Jama, Somali Minister of Information, Culture and Tourism
a1460.name: Daud Aweis Jama
a1460.title: Somali Minister of Information, Culture and Tourism
a1460.speech: Has asked the member countries of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to support Somalia in its position against Ethiopia's interference in the sovereignty and independence of Somalia.

a1460.speaker: Osman Igaal, Somali Minister of Transport and Aviation
a1460.name: Osman Igaal
a1460.title: Somali Minister of Transport and Aviation
a1460.speech: Has affirmed that Somalia's air traffic management operations are functioning securely without any issues.

a1460.speaker: Somali Civil Aviation Authority
a1460.name: Somali Civil Aviation Authority
a1460.speech: Has said that there is any [sic] safety risk in the Somali airspace.

a1460.speaker: Disaster Management Agency of Somalia (report)
a1460.name: Disaster Management Agency of Somalia (report)
a1460.speech: Presented a report on the effects of the rains and floods in Elnino areas of Hirshabelle at a meeting attended by the President of the Hirshabelle State, Mr. Ali Abdullahi Hussein (Ali Guudlawe).

a1490.speaker: Salim Levent Sahinkaya, Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.name: Salim Levent Sahinkaya
a1490.title: Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.speech: Writes that Turkey, with its 83 million inhabitants, its deeply rooted history, its strategic position between Asia and Europe and its developing economy, is one of the most important countries in its region; that Turkey is among the world’s 20 largest economies, has the fifth largest diplomatic and consular network in the world with 252 missions abroad, and conducts a diplomacy that thinks globally but also acts regionally.

a1490.speaker: Salim Levent Sahinkaya, Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.name: Salim Levent Sahinkaya
a1490.title: Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.speech: Writes that Turkey attaches importance to its relations with Africa and continues to expand its diplomatic network on the continent, with missions rising from 12 in 2002 to 43; that the total value of Turkish direct investment in Africa has exceeded 6 billion dollars with more than 1,150 projects; that Turkish official development assistance to Africa between 2005 and 2019 reached nearly 3.5 billion dollars; and that TİKA’s bilateral official development assistance for the continent has exceeded 500 million dollars, while the Turkish Maarif Foundation has provided educational services to more than 14,000 students in 144 schools and 16 dormitories across Africa.

a1490.speaker: Salim Levent Sahinkaya, Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.name: Salim Levent Sahinkaya
a1490.title: Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.speech: Writes that terrorism is a crime against humanity that cannot be associated with any race, ethnicity, faith or geography, that it is a global scourge demanding a global response and solidarity, and that Turkey actively fights terrorism unleashed by any organisation under any pretext. He writes that FETÖ is one such organisation, that Fetullah Gülen is its leader and the mastermind of the failed coup of 15 July 2016 in which his followers killed two hundred and fifty-one people, attempted to assassinate the President, bombed the Grand National Assembly and the Ankara police special operations centre.

a1490.speaker: Salim Levent Sahinkaya, Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.name: Salim Levent Sahinkaya
a1490.title: Ambassador of Turkey to Djibouti
a1490.speech: Writes that Turkey has taken administrative measures and initiated judicial proceedings to restrict FETÖ’s room for manoeuvre abroad, requesting extradition and the freezing of members’ assets; that FETÖ-affiliated schools and educational centres in thirty-eight countries have been closed or taken over, with twenty transferring them to the Maarif Foundation of Turkey; and that 15 July has been named “Democracy and National Unity Day” in Turkey, on whose anniversary “we commemorate our 251 martyrs who sacrificed their lives to defend democracy in Turkey.”

a1490.speaker: Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (43rd session, 19 October 2016)
a1490.name: Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (43rd session
a1490.title: 19 October 2016)
a1490.speech: Declared FETÖ a terrorist organisation; a similar resolution was drafted by the Asian Parliamentary Assembly (APA) on 1 December 2016 and ratified at the 12th conference of the Parliamentary Union of the OIC on 27 January 2017.

a1490.speaker: Supreme Court of Pakistan (verdict of 28 December 2018)
a1490.name: Supreme Court of Pakistan (verdict of 28 December 2018)

a1490.speaker: Four parliamentary groups of political parties in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (joint declaration, 9 August 2019)
a1490.name: Four parliamentary groups of political parties in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (joint declaration
a1490.title: 9 August 2019)
a1490.speech: Issued a joint declaration concerning FETÖ, reiterating the call on Turkey’s allies and partners to take measures against this terrorist organisation and its leader.

a1569.speaker: Dispatch, Liberia Permanent Mission to the IMO (Wednesday, April 25, 2025)
a1569.name: Dispatch
a1569.title: Liberia Permanent Mission to the IMO (Wednesday, April 25, 2025)
a1569.speech: Reported that Liberia has once again demonstrated its leadership at the International Maritime Organization (IMO) by fully settling its 2025 contributions amounting to £5.5 million (US$7.1 million), representing Liberia's assessed share of the IMO's £37.5 million budget for 2025.

a1569.speaker: IMO 33rd Assembly session, Resolution A.1179(33) (December 2023)
a1569.name: IMO 33rd Assembly session
a1569.title: Resolution A.1179(33) (December 2023)
a1569.speech: Approved the IMO's £37.5 million budget for 2025, of which Liberia's payment represents its assessed share.

a1569.speaker: Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe, Sr., Commissioner/CEO of the Liberia Maritime Authority
a1569.name: Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe
a1569.title: Sr., Commissioner/CEO of the Liberia Maritime Authority
a1569.speech: Reaffirms Liberia's continued dedication to the IMO, including the timely payment of dues and other contributions that support the Organization's forward drive. He emphasized Liberia's determination to help ensure that global shipping continues to progress to greater heights.

a1705.speaker: FMDQ Securities Exchange (official forex trading platform data)
a1705.name: FMDQ Securities Exchange (official forex trading platform data)
a1705.speech: Data from the FMDQ Securities Exchange official forex trading platform revealed that the Naira gained N11.17, a 0.7 per cent increase compared to the previous day's trading figure on Thursday, when the local currency closed at N1,485.95 to the Dollar.

a1705.speaker: Olayemi Cardoso, CBN Governor
a1705.name: Olayemi Cardoso
a1705.title: CBN Governor
a1705.speech: Speaking in Abuja on Thursday at the 2025 Monetary Policy Forum, stated that recent reforms in the FX segment had continued to attract foreign investments ; reassured that the apex bank would sustain efforts to ensure continued inflows.

a1731.speaker: Yasmine, 14-year-old Ethiopian migrant girl
a1731.name: Yasmine
a1731.title: 14-year-old Ethiopian migrant girl
a1731.speech: "They let me go when I fell ill and they could no longer use me."

a1731.speaker: Fariida Musse, staff member at Bosaso's Migrant Response Centre (IOM)
a1731.name: Fariida Musse
a1731.title: staff member at Bosaso's Migrant Response Centre (IOM)
a1731.speech: According to Fariida Musse, many women who visit the centre have been held hostage for several months. "Dozens of pregnant women come here alone and don't know what to do with their babies."

a1731.speaker: Franz Celestin, IOM Chief of Mission in Somalia
a1731.name: Franz Celestin
a1731.title: IOM Chief of Mission in Somalia
a1731.speech: Said adequate funding to support migrants could have prevented situations like Yasmine's: "We could have had someone accompany her on the trip back to ensure she had access to the assistance she needed after such a traumatic event."

a1731.speaker: Franz Celestin, IOM Chief of Mission in Somalia
a1731.name: Franz Celestin
a1731.title: IOM Chief of Mission in Somalia
a1731.speech: On reintegration programmes: "Migrants who returned home, thanks to our programme, have received skills training, education courses, grants and medical support" ; "If people had opportunities, they wouldn't be risking their lives and traffickers couldn't take advantage of them."

a1731.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1731.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1731.speech: IOM estimates there are 43,000 migrants trapped in Yemen, living in precarious conditions and at risk of getting caught in the ongoing conflict ; IOM is now appealing for USD 58.5 million through the Migrant Response Plan (MRP) to continue this vital support in the region.

a1816.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a1816.name: Joseph Boakai
a1816.title: President of Liberia
a1816.speech: "The donation of medical supplies will help cater to the medical needs of the citizens, especially women and children in the county." The Liberian Leader reemphasized the Government of Liberia's determination to improve all sectors of society, including the health needs of the citizens. He said the government, through the Health Ministry, will continue to collaborate with development partners to ensure that citizens are healthier and more productive.

a1816.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a1816.name: Joseph Boakai
a1816.title: President of Liberia
a1816.speech: Has emphasized the need to provide opportunities for people to achieve their potential and contribute to the growth of their communities. He also underscored the role of local businesses in creating jobs and economic growth and the benefits of investing in infrastructure like roads and airstrips. He made the statement on Monday, December 22, 2024, when he dedicated the "After the Rain Guest House" in Voinjama City, and called for a collective effort to enhance the quality of life and pride in the country, lauding the management of the facility for the huge initiative.

a1816.speaker: Medical staff and management of Tellewoyan Hospital
a1816.name: Medical staff and management of Tellewoyan Hospital
a1816.speech: Lauded the President for the gesture, terming it as timely.

a2016.speaker: United Nations (report published Wednesday)
a2016.name: United Nations (report published Wednesday)
a2016.speech: The UN has urged the international community to respond to what it called human rights violations by Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega’s government as it seeks to further consolidate power. The UN report accuses Ortega and his wife, Rosario Murillo, who serves as co-president, of having “transformed the country into an authoritarian state where no independent institutions remain” ; the report also implicated the Nicaraguan army in the violent crackdown, contradicting previous denials ; according to the report, the wide-ranging constitutional reform to expand presidential powers has “eliminated what little remained of institutional checks and balances.”

a2016.speaker: UN experts
a2016.name: UN experts
a2016.speech: Urged legal action against Nicaragua, highlighting human rights abuses in the Latin American country, which they said follow patterns that have been previously established as crimes against humanity.

a2016.speaker: Ortega’s government (Nicaragua)
a2016.name: Ortega’s government (Nicaragua)
a2016.speech: Has in the past ignored reports from the UN and the Organisation of American States, which it says are part of an international campaign against it.

a2016.speaker: Government allies (Nicaragua)
a2016.name: Government allies (Nicaragua)
a2016.speech: The reforms have been defended by government allies as deepening a nearly 50-year-old revolution which began in 1979 when Ortega and fellow leftist guerrillas overthrew a right-wing family dynasty.

a2756.speaker: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo", fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.name: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo"
a2756.title: fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.speech: Recalls that as a boy he would watch the boats come back from the sea full of fish - "A lot, a lot of fish" - and that at 13 a fisherman called Ze let him go along, and although he knew nothing of fishing he caught a tuna: "I was happy. The next day I went again, and I caught a tuna and a wahoo." ; Says he took the animals to the Achada early, left them with his colleagues and "ran off to fish", receiving a share of the money the boat owner made from the sale. ; "The sea gave me a living." ; "I have nothing bad to say about the sea, nothing to complain about. I am of the sea. Everything I need I got only from the sea."

a2756.speaker: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo", fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.name: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo"
a2756.title: fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.speech: Observes that there is much less fish today, and offers reasons: first, that "there are many more boats" fishing, and that from the 1990s engines became widespread, allowing fishing in more adverse weather and over longer distances; he also stresses that "there began to be many more buildings" along the coast, that construction brought demand for sand, so that places that once had sandy beaches are now a heap of stones, and that sand is important for the life cycle of fish, so sand extraction contributed to the fall in catches - "Whoever has studied more than me is the one who can speak." ; "Everything that goes to the sea, the sea brings back to the land."

a2756.speaker: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo", fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.name: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo"
a2756.title: fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.speech: "The climate has changed a lot" - January used to be a cold month when everyone complained about low temperatures, especially at night: "These days, the month of January has no cold." ; Says that between May and September there used to be plenty of fish, "bottom fish, surface fish, there was everything, and in quantity. Today there is little fish. Pexi sta poku."

a2756.speaker: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo", fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.name: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo"
a2756.title: fisherman from Tarrafal, Cabo Verde
a2756.speech: On closed seasons: "His bread is there. So it becomes a kind of fight between the authorities and the fishermen, because it touches their bread." ; Advises: "Another move has to be made, compensate the fishermen financially so they don't catch those fish."

a2756.speaker: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo", fisherman and boat-trip operator
a2756.name: Carlos Alberto Varela "Mingo"
a2756.title: fisherman and boat-trip operator
a2756.speech: Says that since 2012 he has rented out his boat for tourist trips - viewing the coast, snorkelling or fishing - after a French friend who owns a hotel in Tarrafal gave him the idea and advertised the service; recalls from a meeting with the Maritime and Port Institute (IMP) that there are now 11 boats registered in Tarrafal for this ecotourism activity, and that the meeting also served as a kind of training on working conditions and required equipment, notably first aid and life jackets. ; "There are times when fishing gives more than tourism, and others when tourism gives more. But when fishing pays, the income is bigger. Sometimes in one day I make 40 or 50 contos and I know people who make up to 100 contos in a day."

a2756.speaker: Tommy Melo, biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.name: Tommy Melo
a2756.title: biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.speech: Explains that coastal zones in Cabo Verde are very small and the country has no "continental shelf like the countries of West Africa, such as Mauritania or Senegal", so with a very small demersal fishing zone that is difficult to recover, "much more applied and serious management" is required to prevent overfishing. ; Notes that species once relatively common are becoming scarce, especially predators, and even the size of the fish caught is falling: "If we look at the average size of a grouper that was caught 20 years ago, it does not correspond to what is caught today. So one sees that the impacts really are being felt in that coastal strip."

a2756.speaker: Tommy Melo, biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.name: Tommy Melo
a2756.title: biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.speech: On sand extraction: "A sandy beach takes thousands of years to form. So the ecosystem that lives there also took thousands of years to adapt to sandy bottoms. There are many species that need sandy bottoms for their life cycle, whether for reproduction, because they live close to the sandy substrate, or for other reasons. Obviously, removing in 10 years all the sand from a beach that took thousands of years to form will cause an imbalance in the ecosystem, particularly in those species." ; "Hydrodynamism in coastal zones is already something that is stable. The tidal cycles themselves, the annual seasonal cycles, mean that sometimes the sand is taken from one place and put in another, but it comes back. We are talking about cycles of thousands of years. So human interference in ending that sand deposit in so short a time really does have an impact, given that biodiversity cannot adapt at a rate as fast as the changes being imposed by man."

a2756.speaker: Tommy Melo, biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.name: Tommy Melo
a2756.title: biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.speech: Explains that the change in temperature means "some shoals move mostly further north in search of colder waters".

a2756.speaker: Tommy Melo, biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.name: Tommy Melo
a2756.title: biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.speech: On solutions: "They are management solutions, purely, and there is no need to reinvent the wheel here. They already exist, they have long been applied in other countries." ; "You need rest zones, you need effective marine reserves and enforcement that really happens." ; Recommends that "the government has to look for alternative sources of income for those families who will be left without that subsistence because the fishing zones they used to use really have to rest in order to recover the fauna that existed."

a2756.speaker: Tommy Melo, biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.name: Tommy Melo
a2756.title: biologist, environmentalist and president of Biosfera
a2756.speech: Warns on tourism that "we are wearing down the environment much faster than we can use it for tourism", citing sand extraction that destroys beaches, damaging construction on the shoreline, and continuing overfishing without "regulation really being enforced": "That is to say, we are on a parallel path in which, if we do not start taking measures, even the potential that Cabo Verde may have for tourism development and for attracting tourists may be lost before we even begin to use it."

a2756.speaker: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne", tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.name: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne"
a2756.title: tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.speech: Says that for tourists who like to fish it is always a great joy when they manage to catch a fish, but whether for leisure or as a primary source of income there is less and less fish: "Before we caught 10 tuna, now it is one, sometimes two."

a2756.speaker: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne", tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.name: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne"
a2756.title: tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.speech: "We fishermen are somewhat abandoned because we do not have much support. We have support for the engine and for the boat, but we needed support at the level of new fishing technologies", citing the need for "equipment such as a sounder with GPS". ; Says he also lacks support and training in awareness of climate change and its impacts, notably on currents: "We have recorded recently, in our fishing zone, that from time to time there is a cold water current and a warm water current; it is not normal. One day hot, one day cold. One day with fish, one day without fish." ; Considers there is a need for more training on fish species - which are endemic, which are protected, what size they should be: "The fisherman must know all that; if we do not know it we will finish off the marine ecosystem itself, we will finish off everything."

a2756.speaker: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne", tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.name: Nelito Semedo Tavares "Ne"
a2756.title: tour operator, lifeguard and fisherman, Tarrafal
a2756.speech: Recounts that in 2019 he took part in a blue entrepreneurship competition promoted by Pro-Empresa: "I reached the final, in Sao Vicente"; says he now has a business plan ready to apply but lacks financing, the bank having told him he needs 20 per cent of the 7,000 contos foreseen to unlock a loan. ; "I wanted to have a sport fishing boat so I could take part in the Blue Marlin fishing championships here in Cabo Verde, and also fish with tourists. For example, go with them as far as the coast of Maio. That is my dream. I hope that one day I can get there."

a2756.speaker: Report on Development and Climate Change (CCDR), World Bank
a2756.name: Report on Development and Climate Change (CCDR)
a2756.title: World Bank
a2756.speech: States that "creating a climate-adapted blue economy is at the heart of Cabo Verde's development plans", stressing that the country's beaches and marine fauna are fundamental to "tourism and fisheries, pillars of the economy"; recalls that tourism generates 25% of GDP and 45% of formal-sector jobs and faces challenges such as rising temperatures "and the environmental impact of poorly planned coastal development", and that fisheries - the second largest source of dietary protein and 72% of exports in 2021 - suffer from overfishing and poor management, harming both fishermen's incomes and access to seafood; says it is essential to create protection zones, regulate catch techniques and explore new forms of production such as aquaculture and seaweed cultivation, and recommends, among seven strategic objectives, to "Develop a climate-resilient blue economy", supporting research and monitoring of fishery resources, promoting sustainable fishing with regulations, no-take regeneration zones and standards/certifications for processed products while increasing aquaculture, diversifying tourism beyond sun and beach, and protecting coastal ecosystems and encouraging private-sector climate adaptation.

a2775.speaker: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.name: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.speech: Said the ministers are also set to discuss modalities for the operationalisation of its Humanitarian and Emergency Operations Centre (SHOC) as well as to review progress made towards the operationalisation of the Regional Appeal for Humanitarian Assistance: "The Committee of Ministers Responsible for Disaster Risk Management (DRM) from the Southern African Development Community (SADC) will meet in Victoria Falls, Republic of Zimbabwe, on 27 November 2024. During the meeting, ministers will review progress on the implementation of regional disaster management activities and programmes aimed at strengthening the region's preparedness and response to disasters."

a2775.speaker: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.name: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.speech: Said the launch of the appeal for aid follows the negative impacts of the El Nino induced drought and floods that negatively affected the lives and livelihoods of an estimated 58 million people in SADC countries that provided data.

a2775.speaker: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.name: SADC Secretariat (statement)
a2775.speech: Said the ministers will further consider an Addendum to the Regional Appeal that has been prepared following the finalisation of vulnerability assessments by additional Member States that had not finalised their assessments at the time the appeal was launched in May.

a2792.speaker: Civil Society Advocacy Forum (Csaf) (statement/analysis)
a2792.name: Civil Society Advocacy Forum (Csaf) (statement/analysis)
a2792.speech: Says its analysis of health sector proposals outlined in the manifestos of various political parties has revealed substantial gaps in understanding and commitment to addressing specific needs of the health sector. A statement on the analysis notes that many political parties and independent candidates lack a comprehensive understanding of the current challenges facing the health sector in the context of the prevailing global funding and priorities.

a2792.speaker: People's Party (PP) manifesto
a2792.name: People's Party (PP) manifesto
a2792.speech: Proposes to implement new health financing strategies such as levies on alcohol and tobacco products to augment national budgetary allocations. It also plans to establish a national health fund to manage the alternative health finances, improve health service delivery and explore the feasibility of introducing a compulsory national health insurance scheme.

a2792.speaker: UTM Party manifesto
a2792.name: UTM Party manifesto
a2792.speech: Does not outline specific sources of funds, but says its regime would provide free essential services at all public facilities, hire more nurses, midwives, and doctors, fix drug supply systems and expand rural clinics.

a2792.speaker: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) manifesto
a2792.name: Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) manifesto
a2792.speech: Says it will “introduce health fund and universal health coverage to support health financing”.

a2792.speaker: United Democratic Front (UDF) manifesto
a2792.name: United Democratic Front (UDF) manifesto
a2792.speech: Argues that Malawi's budgetary allocation is one of the most generous in the region. “We must have a more honest and detailed discussion about health financing that takes a more comprehensive view of the whole sector,” it says.

a2792.speaker: Malawi Congress Party (MCP) manifesto
a2792.name: Malawi Congress Party (MCP) manifesto
a2792.speech: Says it will create a National Health Services Fund (NHSF). “The NHSF shall be capitalized through levies on alcohol, cigarettes, phone calls, financial services and fuel,” it says.

a2792.speaker: Civil Society Advocacy Forum (Csaf) (statement)
a2792.name: Civil Society Advocacy Forum (Csaf) (statement)
a2792.speech: Argues that recent cuts in donor aid have exacerbated existing challenges such as inadequate access to essential services, increased vulnerability among marginalised populations, and a decline in the quality of healthcare services. Reads Csaf statement: “While a few parties have mentioned strategies to finance the health sector in their manifestos, most have not clearly explained plans on how they will domestically mobilise for the health sector. Political Parties and independent candidates are failing to recognise health as part of human capital development as such they are not prioritizing or mentioning the allocations to be made to the health sector.” Further, it argues that some parties are operating within the traditional comfort zone that has influenced donor dependence over the years, challenging their ability to propose innovative strategies for a turnaround in health financing.

a2792.speaker: Gift Trapence, Csaf chairperson
a2792.name: Gift Trapence
a2792.title: Csaf chairperson
a2792.speech: Called on political parties and independent candidates to provide clear strategies on how their potential administration would locally generate resources to finance the health sector. He said: “The country must prioritise generating domestic resources to fund the health sector rather than heavily relying on external support.”

a2792.speaker: United Kingdom government (announcement)
a2792.name: United Kingdom government (announcement)
a2792.speech: Last month, the United Kingdom announced a decision to cut foreign aid to sectors such as health to 11 countries, including Malawi, putting the country at risk as funding to the area is largely dependent on donors.

a3002.speaker: President of Ghana
a3002.name: President of Ghana
a3002.speech: Is particularly concerned about the potential $78.2 million shortfall, which will have a detrimental effect on critical interventions, including malaria prevention, maternal and child health, family planning, reproductive health, nutrition and the fight against HIV/AIDS.

a3143.speaker: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.name: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye
a3143.title: Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.speech: has revealed that her life was under danger over her efforts to rid the country of fake and illicit drug products; said she doesn’t have a life anymore, as she has no freedom to move the way she pleases without security protection; said her staff who assist to make her job meaningful are also facing security threats, giving account of how one of her staff member’s son was kidnapped, but luckily escaped from the abductors ; “I told you about the attempted murder about six months ago. One of our staff in Kano, his child was kidnapped because the father was doing what he was supposed to do. Fortunately the child escaped. For me, I have two policemen living in my house 24/7 in Abuja and Lagos. I don’t have a life. I cannot go anywhere without police and to me that is not my way of living. But I don’t have a choice because we’ve got to save our country. Nonetheless, I also use common sense.”

a3143.speaker: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.name: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye
a3143.title: Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.speech: Speaking on the controversies trailing recent seizures in some drug markets within the country, she said the recent large-scale enforcement operation across three major open drug markets of Onitsha, Aba and Lagos, will pass as one of the biggest seizures in NAFDAC’s history; she estimated the total drugs and counterfeit products seized at about N1 trillion and said the value could be much higher after assessment; said it was part of NAFDAC’s National Action Plan (NAP 2.0) 2023-2027, aimed at eliminating counterfeit medicines, improving regulatory compliance, and safeguarding public health; revealed that the exercise, which commenced on February 9, 2025, involved 1,100 security operatives, including military personnel, police, and Department of State Services (DSS) agents, and that the security forces cordoned off the markets to prevent traders from concealing or smuggling out illegal products.

a3143.speaker: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.name: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye
a3143.title: Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.speech: said the ongoing crackdown on illicit drug trade by operatives of the agency has also resulted in the seizure of 87 truckloads of banned, expired, and substandard medical products, including USAID and UNFPA-donated antiretroviral drugs, male and female condoms; affirmed that the operation uncovered shocking violations of drug storage and distribution regulations, including diverted donated medical supplies, large quantities of USAID and UNFPA-donated antiretroviral drugs and condoms meant to support Nigeria’s HIV/AIDS response found expired and repackaged for sale; said these life-saving medications were either improperly stored or deliberately resold for profit, undermining global efforts to combat HIV/AIDS in Nigeria.

a3143.speaker: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.name: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye
a3143.title: Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.speech: said the sheer volume of narcotics seized – Tramadol, Flunitrazepam (Rohypnol), Nitrazepam, and Diazepam – was deemed sufficient to destabilise national security; said a large quantity of Tafradol, recently banned in India after a BBC undercover investigation exposed its illicit export to Africa, was discovered in Onitsha, and that the drug, unapproved anywhere in the world, has been widely abused in Nigeria; noted that vaccines, prescription medicines, and thermolabile drugs were found stacked in toilets, staircases, and rooftops at dangerously high temperatures; disclosed that banned and expired drugs were hidden in plumbing and wood plank sections of Onitsha’s Bridge Head Market, while unregistered and falsified products were found in over 7,000 shops screened during the operation.

a3143.speaker: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.name: Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye
a3143.title: Director General of NAFDAC
a3143.speech: announced that so far, 40 arrests have been made, with suspects facing prosecution; urged the National Assembly to develop the will to enact death penalty or life imprisonment for peddlers of fake and counterfeit drugs in the country, saying such punitive measure is the only way for perpetrators to atone for their wickedness, especially the level of fake and counterfeit products in circulation in the country.

a3277.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a3277.name: Barack Obama
a3277.title: President of the United States
a3277.speech: Declared on 4 November 2008: "I do not underestimate the enormity of the task that lies before us," before setting out the essentials of his programme.

a3277.speaker: Hillary Clinton, US Secretary of State
a3277.name: Hillary Clinton
a3277.title: US Secretary of State
a3277.speech: Declared on Monday 2 November: "The Obama administration's position on the settlements is clear, unequivocal. It has not changed: the United States does not accept the legitimacy of the continuation of Israeli settlements."

a3277.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a3277.name: Barack Obama
a3277.title: President of the United States
a3277.speech: In his Cairo speech on 4 June, asked Tel Aviv "that the settlement building cease" in the Palestinian territories, settlement building which "violates past agreements and undermines peace efforts"; repeated that his country supports the "legitimate" aspirations of the Palestinians to a State and that the "only solution" is the one that provides for two States; and tirelessly advocates the resumption of negotiations.

a3277.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a3277.name: Barack Obama
a3277.title: President of the United States
a3277.speech: In a video message subtitled in Farsi broadcast for the Iranian new year on 19 March, called on Iran and the United States to "overcome their old divisions."

a3277.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a3277.name: Barack Obama
a3277.title: President of the United States
a3277.speech: On 28 February confirmed the withdrawal of American troops from Iraq before the end of 2011, saying he wants to redeploy them, essentially in Afghanistan.

a3277.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a3277.name: Barack Obama
a3277.title: President of the United States
a3277.speech: Promised that he would go all the way on the announced closure of the Guantanamo prison, even if the closure will happen later than the planned "within the first 100 days of his presidency."

a3277.speaker: Washington / the White House (US government)
a3277.name: Washington / the White House (US government)
a3277.speech: Announced on 24 June its decision to send an ambassador to Syria again, and on 27 July made a gesture towards Syria by easing the pressure of American trade sanctions.

a3277.speaker: Nobel Peace Prize citation (Norwegian Nobel Committee)
a3277.name: Nobel Peace Prize citation (Norwegian Nobel Committee)
a3277.speech: Awarded the prize in the name of "his efforts to strengthen diplomacy and cooperation between peoples" and for his "efforts towards a world without nuclear weapons."

a3320.speaker: Mamunie Dennis, Board Chairlady, All-Liberian Diaspora Women Organization (ALDWO)
a3320.name: Mamunie Dennis
a3320.title: Board Chairlady, All-Liberian Diaspora Women Organization (ALDWO)
a3320.speech: Said back in 2018, when she and others started, they just had a vision of service to their communities; she further stated that they did not think about themselves but thought about others and what they could do to make the Liberian Community in the US better. “But somewhere along the way, we realized that there are people who have done well, and we needed to recognize those people” ; described him as standing for positivity and strong in advocacy: “We all enjoy dual citizenship today; he is one of the forces behind dual citizenship. Even when he left ULAA, he never stopped his advocacy.”

a3320.speaker: One of the ladies who gowned the Eminent Chairman
a3320.name: One of the ladies who gowned the Eminent Chairman
a3320.speech: Beseeched God’s guidance upon him for the many sacrifices he made and continues to make for the Liberian Community in the USA.

a3320.speaker: ALDWO award plaque (inscription)
a3320.name: ALDWO award plaque (inscription)
a3320.speech: “In recognition of a lifetime of unwavering dedication, exceptional service, and outstanding contributions to advocating [for] community issues; your tireless efforts have a profound and lasting impact, championing causes that have uplifted countless individuals and strengthened communities. Through your leadership and commitment, you have inspired positive change, fostering an environment of progress and unity. Your legacy of advocacy continues to guide and motivate others to follow in your footsteps, ensuring a brighter future for all.”

a3320.speaker: Emmanuel Sonnyboy Wettee, Eminent Chairman of the All-Liberian Conference on Dual Citizenship (ALCOD)
a3320.name: Emmanuel Sonnyboy Wettee
a3320.title: Eminent Chairman of the All-Liberian Conference on Dual Citizenship (ALCOD)
a3320.speech: Thanked everyone who thought about him and specifically mentioned Mr. Alfred Sieh, whom he shared the award with: “This is the man, who if you call me to go to Liberia to advocate for dual citizenship or out-of-country voting, he is willing to purchase his own ticket, at price of 2 to US$3,000 a trip to go with me. This man has stood with me throughout the advocacy. We have gone to Liberia on many occasions. Mr. Sieh, today, I want to share this honor with you, your wife and with the ULAA Family. I thank you for supporting me” ; concluded his statement of gratitude by pledging US$1,000 to ALDWO’s initiatives.

a3320.speaker: Emmanuel Sonnyboy Wettee, then head of ULAA (inaugural address, December 2005)
a3320.name: Emmanuel Sonnyboy Wettee
a3320.title: then head of ULAA (inaugural address, December 2005)
a3320.speech: Promised no Liberian would be deported under his watch, when about 10,000 Liberians on TPS were supposed to be deported.

a3320.speaker: Kartumu Y. Boakai, First Lady of Liberia
a3320.name: Kartumu Y. Boakai
a3320.title: First Lady of Liberia
a3320.speech: “We are so proud of you. The idea that you came here, despite losing your mother, shows that Liberia is above all” ; “Your love and passion for our country are evident. Please accept our sympathy on behalf of the President and the people of Liberia. Thank you for all your sacrifices” ; applauded his selflessness and patriotism.

a3320.speaker: UNHCR
a3320.name: UNHCR
a3320.speech: Applauded Liberia for removing gender discrimination from its nationality law.

a3446.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia
a3446.name: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia
a3446.speech: Requested 415 million dollars from the International Monetary Fund through the Rapid Disbursement Instrument Facility without ex-post conditionality, in response to the economic impact of COVID-19.

a3446.speaker: Abebe Amero Selassie, Director of the IMF for Africa
a3446.name: Abebe Amero Selassie
a3446.title: Director of the IMF for Africa
a3446.speech: Said in a web press briefing on Wednesday that together with the World Bank the IMF is making a case for debt relief from official bilateral creditors for those low-income countries that can make their case: "Aside from the current underway supports, the IMF is seeking resources to avail grants to countries with debt service payments that fail for the remaining time of the year."

a3446.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a3446.name: Eyob Tekalign (PhD)
a3446.title: State Minister for Finance of Ethiopia
a3446.speech: "Although the amount may not look substantial, we have asked for debt relief alongside the 415 million dollar emergency fund" ; "Ethiopia will get debt relief, and the Rapid Disbursement Facility request will process it."

a3446.speaker: International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook)
a3446.name: International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook)
a3446.speech: Slashed the prospective growth of Ethiopia for the current fiscal year by half from its previous projection of 6.2pc, and stated the impact of COVID-19 is appearing through costs to humanity worldwide, and that the protective actions have severely impacted the economic ecosystem.

a3446.speaker: Cepheus Growth Capital (study by the Ethiopian private equity firm)
a3446.name: Cepheus Growth Capital (study by the Ethiopian private equity firm)
a3446.speech: Estimates growth will be 2.5 percentage points lower next year, falling to five percent; estimates that fiscal resources needed for public relief packages could reach 90 billion Br, 2.3pc of GDP, and that central bank liquidity interventions of around 47 billion Br, 1.2pc of GDP, may be required; also estimates the impact of the pandemic would be at the higher cap of one percentage point of GDP for the current fiscal year.

a3446.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a3446.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a3446.speech: Estimates the minimum expenditure for the prevention of the pandemic is expected to be five billion Br in the best-case scenario, which can go up to 19 billion Br under the worst-case scenario.

a3607.speaker: Indian business delegation in Maputo
a3607.name: Indian business delegation in Maputo
a3607.speech: A delegation of businesspeople from India, from various lines of activity, expressed today in Maputo their interest in exploring more business opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry, energy, mining, agribusiness and others.

a3607.speaker: Robert Sheki Shetkintong, High Commissioner of India in Mozambique
a3607.name: Robert Sheki Shetkintong
a3607.title: High Commissioner of India in Mozambique
a3607.speech: said that the sharing of experiences between the business sectors of India and Mozambique reaffirms the commitment to facilitate relations, promoting a favourable business environment with mutual benefits. “May this be the beginning of new partnerships and concrete opportunities for both countries,” said Shetkintong, speaking in Maputo during the Business Networking event with Mozambican businesspeople.

a3607.speaker: Álvaro Massingue, President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.name: Álvaro Massingue
a3607.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.speech: presented the opportunities the country offers in the various strategic sectors that can leverage the economy and promote inclusive sustainable development. “We reinforce the need for structuring investments in all areas of our economy, with a special focus on the pharmaceutical, agribusiness, mining, industrial and commercial sectors,” he said.

a3607.speaker: Álvaro Massingue, President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.name: Álvaro Massingue
a3607.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.speech: explained that the pharmaceutical sector represents a market of great relevance, not only to guarantee access to essential medicines, but also to promote local industrialization and reduce dependence on imports; for that reason the country is open to partners interested in making possible the transfer of technologies, national production and the efficient distribution of health products.

a3607.speaker: Álvaro Massingue, President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.name: Álvaro Massingue
a3607.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.speech: stressed that agribusiness is one of the pillars of the Mozambican economy, as a way of guaranteeing food security and strengthening value chains. “We have fertile land with more than 36 million hectares, a favourable climate and a growing market; nevertheless, we need investment to modernize production, improve logistics and add value to our agricultural products, making them more competitive on the global market,” he said.

a3607.speaker: Álvaro Massingue, President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.name: Álvaro Massingue
a3607.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.speech: explained, on the mining sector, that the country has reserves of minerals of great importance, including coal, graphite, heavy sands and other strategic resources. “We intend to attract more investments that are not limited to the extraction of these resources, but that also drive their local transformation, generating employment and promoting the development of associated infrastructure,” he said.

a3607.speaker: Álvaro Massingue, President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.name: Álvaro Massingue
a3607.title: President of the Chamber of Commerce of Mozambique
a3607.speech: added that the commercial sector constitutes the backbone of economic connectivity between Mozambique and its international partners, with an expanding market and a strategic position in the SADC region, and that the country has the potential to become a commercial reference point, above all with investments in infrastructure, logistics and the digitalization of commercial processes.

a3618.speaker: Marjorie Munyonga, ZINWA head of corporate communications and marketing
a3618.name: Marjorie Munyonga
a3618.title: ZINWA head of corporate communications and marketing
a3618.speech: Said in an update that the Presidential Rural Development Programme continues to register significant progress, with a total of 416 village, school and youth business units established to date — 41 in the Midlands, six in Harare, 57 in Mashonaland Central, 28 in Mashonaland West, 62 in Mashonaland East, 30 in Matabeleland South, 36 in Matabeleland North, 13 in Bulawayo, 96 in Masvingo and 45 in Manicaland — and that 3,277 boreholes were drilled as of October 30, with 1,695 already equipped with solar systems and bush pumps: “The positive impact of the programme on communities is already being seen with some beneficiaries already having received dividends of up to US$3 000, while others are earning up to US$50 per month from selling their produce to local businesses, boarding schools and supermarkets.”

a3650.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.), macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.name: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.)
a3650.title: macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.speech: According to him, considering the current fiscal year's budget, the proposed budget does not have a significant increase ; “Given the inflation pressure in the economy, the budget isn't expansionary.”

a3650.speaker: Central Statistical Agency (Consumer Price Index)
a3650.name: Central Statistical Agency (Consumer Price Index)
a3650.speech: According to the latest Consumer Price Index, the 12-month moving average inflation rate of the country was 12.6pc as of May 2019.

a3650.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance
a3650.name: Ahmed Shide
a3650.title: Minister of Finance
a3650.speech: Said in statements made to parliament two weeks ago that while preparing the budget bill, the Ministry prepared a five-year macroeconomic and fiscal framework ; “We've also evaluated the budget utilisation of the current and the past fiscal year while preparing the current one” ; “The budget bill is prepared by prioritising water and roads infrastructure.”

a3650.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.), macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.name: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.)
a3650.title: macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.speech: The government's plan of covering three-quarters of the budget from domestic revenue seems unrealistic: “It doesn't consider the actual tax revenue collection of the government. Knowing that the government wouldn't collect the targeted revenue of the year, they should not plan to increase the share of domestic revenue as the source of budget.” ; according to him, with the current capacity of domestic tax revenue, the government could need a supplementary budget.

a3650.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance
a3650.name: Ahmed Shide
a3650.title: Minister of Finance
a3650.speech: Says the Finance Ministry expects the revenue collection of the country to go up by 20 billion Br to 30 billion Br after the ongoing tax regime reform is completed ; “We're revising value-added and excise tax proclamations along with tax reforms to tax holiday and incentive privileges, which all will increase government revenue and improve tax administration” ; adds that the government will be focusing on controlling expenses in the coming fiscal year.

a3650.speaker: A macroeconomist with a wide range of experience (unnamed)
a3650.name: A macroeconomist with a wide range of experience (unnamed)
a3650.speech: Believes that the spending devised in the budget document is unproductive, huge and inflationary: “It shows that there is a bloated bureaucracy. Despite the Auditor General's report, the budget doesn't properly allocate productive spending.”

a3650.speaker: Office of the Auditor General (latest audit finding)
a3650.name: Office of the Auditor General (latest audit finding)
a3650.speech: Shows that in the last fiscal year there was 1.6 million Br cash on balance, six billion Birr in uncollected receivable cash, seven billion Birr in uncollected tax revenue and seven billion Birr of uncleared expenditures in the government accounts.

a3650.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a3650.name: Experts (unnamed)
a3650.speech: Warn the government to watch the debt level of the country carefully.

a3650.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.), macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.name: Alemayehu Geda (Prof.)
a3650.title: macroeconomist and university professor
a3650.speech: Still believes that the country should search for a grant to escape from a budget deficit and supplementary budget, but says the grant has to be used for the procurement of essential goods like wheat instead of injecting it into the economy ; “If the grant is converted into local currency and injected into the economy it could cause inflation. In the long run, the country has to work a lot in building its capacity for revenue collection.”

a3712.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.name: Chris Appiah
a3712.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.speech: Says this is an initiative of the ECOWAS Commission, through its President, in collaboration with the African Development Bank, to give back to the 400 million people living within the West African region ; emphasizes that ECOWAS wants to ease difficulties in movements along corridors of African countries beginning from Cape Verse, Gambia, Senegal, Guinea, Guinea Beusa, Liberia, and Ivory Coast and ending in Nigeria and Central Africa: “So at the level of ECOWAS, we want to make sure these corridors are connected without missing lands in order for our citizens to have free movement and trade among themselves” ; “So as you can see, this area is one of the major missing Lands or corridors that starts from Dakar to Abuja, although there are other crossing points, this point of Cavalla is a major point.”

a3712.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.name: Chris Appiah
a3712.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
