a3712.speech: Discloses that the African Development Bank has consented to finance the US$258M Cavalla River bridge and connecting roads so that citizens of both sides can freely move about and solidify regional trade and integration ; reveals that they have gone through a process of selecting contractors that was inclusive, with engineers from Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire participating in picking a contractor from China who has been awarded the contract for the construction of the bridge ; adds that the project is expected to be completed in 24 months or two years ; points out that the designs of the bridge took into consideration all necessary site situations, design principles, and factors to avoid possible occurrences that had happened or that could affect the project: “So as you can see from the site, it's a very difficult site however, but during the design period, several visits were paid on this site to access the level of the River and the nature of the terrain in order to build a design that will fate in this form.”

a3712.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.name: Chris Appiah
a3712.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.speech: “We are also here with the engineers from Ivory Coast, and it's unfortunate engineers from Liberia aren't present, but perhaps they will join us because this project needs proper supervision on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis” ; underscores that ECOWAS is currently working with the two countries (Liberia and Ivory Coast) to ensure the project's success because its success depends on proper supervision: “So to have it done, we have consultants from ECOWAS, and they are responsible for monitoring the contractors and making sure the contracts are done in accordance with the agreement” ; stresses that they are counting on Liberia and Côte d'Ivoire to provide supervision because supervision is the major factor in every engineering work, and both countries are to provide two engineers each to work with supervisors to ensure the project is done ; says construction materials for the bridge would be transported through the port of Liberia or Ivory Coast, and they will need the support of both countries to facilitate the clearance of materials to be taken to the project site.

a3712.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.name: Chris Appiah
a3712.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.speech: Discloses that ECOWAS is still pursuing its goal of integration despite political challenges, and they would ensure that the economic side, which has been put in place through infrastructure, is done to enable the Community to move and travel freely and act as one region ; reiterates that the project aims to create an economic union that will enable people to move freely, establish businesses in other African countries as if they were citizens of those countries, and intermarry ; says over 400 million people reside in West Africa, a big market, but that road connectivity within the ECOWAS region is needed because roads do 90% of trading: “So as ECOWAS tries to find all the missing lands in the road network, it has been a problem, and here's where the project comes to be able to break the constraints for the 400 Million people within the region because we know people are living within these countries are interdependence in terms of Education, Agriculture, Tourism, Environment, and all these Economic sectors; infrastructure is the main catalyst to have it done.”

a3712.speaker: Chris Appiah, Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.name: Chris Appiah
a3712.title: Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission
a3712.speech: Reveals that as part of ECOWAS' success stories, they have completed a US$400m bridge between Nigeria and Cameroon, and says that because of that, trade within that region has improved; he believes if a similar thing is done here, it will further enhance regional trade and movements because ECOWAS believes in border crossing infrastructure, stressing that ECOWAS has been working with several countries to construct joint border posts, which is currently happening between Ghana and Togo ; disclosed that the official groundbreaking ceremony is scheduled for November and is expected to bring together President Joseph Nyuma Boakai and his counterpart from the Ivory Coast.

a3712.speaker: David Leo, Project Manager of SHAANXI Construction Engineering Corporation LTD
a3712.name: David Leo
a3712.title: Project Manager of SHAANXI Construction Engineering Corporation LTD
a3712.speech: Lauds ECOWAS and the team of delegates for the trust imposed in their company and promises that they will work within the timeframe set ; emphasizes that the best and only way to complete the project smoothly is for both countries to provide support and cooperation.

a3712.speaker: Henry Cole, Maryland County Superintendent
a3712.name: Henry Cole
a3712.title: Maryland County Superintendent
a3712.speech: Applauds ECOWAS and delegates for such a promising opportunity, assuring that his office and the people of Liberia will do everything possible to provide support for the project ; is optimistic the project will bring total relief to his people, as they face difficulties in accessing goods and services from the neighbouring country.

a3772.speaker: Ericson Z. Mechian, Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.name: Ericson Z. Mechian
a3772.title: Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.speech: Said the foundation's operations will target key sectors including health, education, and emergency response; emphasised that AFEE seeks to complement government efforts in bridging service delivery gaps, particularly those resulting from recent USAID funding cuts: "This is not just a foundation. We have come to support government initiatives by collaborating with like-minded organizations to maximize impact and promote a culture of lifelong learning."

a3772.speaker: Ericson Z. Mechian, Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.name: Ericson Z. Mechian
a3772.title: Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.speech: "Education is a powerful tool, and we are using it to unlock the potential of every child. We want to empower individuals to overcome socioeconomic barriers and reach their full potential."

a3772.speaker: Ericson Z. Mechian, Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.name: Ericson Z. Mechian
a3772.title: Secretary General of the Amara Foundation for Education and Empowerment (AFEE)
a3772.speech: On the foundation's exploration of partnership agreements with recognised colleges and universities, local and international: "This proposed partnership will create a vibrant learning environment where less fortunate children can learn, grow, and succeed."

a3850.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a3850.name: Cesar Chelala
a3850.title: global health consultant
a3850.speech: stated that although Africa bears one-quarter of the global burden of disease, it only has 2% of the world's doctors.

a3850.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a3850.name: Cesar Chelala
a3850.title: global health consultant
a3850.speech: further noted that there has been a sharp increase in non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, cancer and heart and lung diseases.

a3850.speaker: World Health Organization
a3850.name: World Health Organization
a3850.speech: estimates that NCDs will rise in the region by 27% over the next 10 years, resulting in 28 million additional deaths.

a3850.speaker: Dr. Crick Lund, Professor of Psychiatry and Mental Health at the University of Cape Town
a3850.name: Dr. Crick Lund
a3850.title: Professor of Psychiatry and Mental Health at the University of Cape Town
a3850.speech: “By neglecting mental health, it will be difficult to attain many of the Sustainable Development Goals related to poverty, malaria, gender empowerment and education.”

a3850.speaker: Sanjeev Ahluwalia, Advisor, Observer Research Foundation in India
a3850.name: Sanjeev Ahluwalia
a3850.title: Advisor, Observer Research Foundation in India
a3850.speech: argued that health problems are worsened by the lack of health professionals, due in part to the continuing exodus of doctors and nurses to industrialized nations. If health care systems are to be effective, resources must be redirected from curative care in urban settings with high tech equipment to primary and preventive health care.

a3850.speaker: Kar and Cartwright-Smith (study)
a3850.name: Kar and Cartwright-Smith (study)
a3850.speech: According to Kar and Cartwright-Smith, Africa is estimated to have lost in excess of $1 trillion in illicit financial flows. This amount is roughly equivalent to all of the official development assistance received by Africa during the same timeframe.

a3850.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a3850.name: Cesar Chelala
a3850.title: global health consultant
a3850.speech: noted that lack of reliable statistics is a hindrance to improving health systems in Africa. They range from defective systems for civil registration to poor data on maternal and child health indicators, including immunization rates for the most common diseases.

a3850.speaker: World Bank study
a3850.name: World Bank study
a3850.speech: showed that half the population of African countries had not been included in a census.

a3850.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a3850.name: Cesar Chelala
a3850.title: global health consultant
a3850.speech: According to Cesar Chelala they need their human resources to be trained in their own countries. They need more help in preventing major diseases. They need more education for all age levels and they need better conditions of trade for their products. African countries do not need more monetary aid given irresponsibly, which ends up in the hands of government officials and members of the countries' elites.

a3850.speaker: Paul Theroux, writer
a3850.name: Paul Theroux
a3850.title: writer
a3850.speech: wrote about Bono, “There are probably more annoying things than being hectored about African development by a wealthy Irish rock star in a cowboy hat, but I can't think of one at the moment.”

a3857.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Minister of Finance and National Planning of Zambia
a3857.name: Situmbeko Musokotwane
a3857.title: Minister of Finance and National Planning of Zambia
a3857.speech: says Zambia will continue implementing effective fiscal economic reforms and good governance practices to ensure the country gets back on a positive trajectory; said Government will continue strengthening the unfolding economic landscape being experienced in the country ; “Despite the positive gains within a short period of just two years after our New Dawn administration took office, we will not relent and relax.” ; “The time is now to start the real work of restoring economic growth, hence our resolve and focus on implementing robust fiscal and effective economic reforms, coupled with prudent management of resources and good governance practices to ensure quick recovery.”

a3857.speaker: World Economic Outlook, released by Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas, IMF economic counsellor and director of research
a3857.name: World Economic Outlook
a3857.title: released by Pierre-Olivier Gourinchas, IMF economic counsellor and director of research
a3857.speech: projected that Zambia and other sub-Saharan African countries will record growth of between 3.8 percent and over four percent next year.

a3857.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Minister of Finance and National Planning of Zambia
a3857.name: Situmbeko Musokotwane
a3857.title: Minister of Finance and National Planning of Zambia
a3857.speech: says Zambia has made good progress in concluding a marathon debt restructuring and is confident of soon striking agreements with its remaining creditors ; “We expect the deal to be done in months” ; “I am very confident that we have made a lot of progress” ; told Bloomberg that a recent visit to China by a delegation from Zambia had been “extremely productive”.

a3857.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3857.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a3857.speech: says it remains committed to supporting Zambia and other sub-Saharan African countries to navigate through climate shocks causing drought and other negative impacts on economies and people.

a3857.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a3857.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a3857.title: President of Zambia
a3857.speech: appealed to local and international partners to help finance the over K23 billion needed to mitigate the impact of drought in the country that has adversely affected 9.8 million people.

a3857.speaker: Julie Kozack, IMF spokesperson
a3857.name: Julie Kozack
a3857.title: IMF spokesperson
a3857.speech: has noted that over the last several years and decades, an increased frequency of climate shocks has intensified globally ; “And Africa has been particularly hard hit by these climate shocks, and we see this, of course, happening now with these droughts in Zimbabwe, Malawi, and Zambia.” ; “The IMF remains committed to supporting sub-Saharan African countries. These successive shocks, including climate shocks, have underscored the importance of the IMF's role as an essential component to sub-Saharan Africa's safety net, particularly for countries with limited policy buffers.” ; “Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, the IMF has provided almost US$58 billion worth of financing to sub-Saharan Africa, most of it on highly concessional terms. And with respect to supporting countries building resilience to climate shocks, there are currently nine countries in sub-Saharan Africa that have arrangements approved under our resilience and sustainability facility.” ; “And we have received many more requests for support under this instrument, and we will continue to work with countries.”

a3927.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a3927.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.speech: Says the cost for the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID) plan is nearly US$8.4 billion, of which 30 percent will be funded by the Government of Liberia, while the remaining 70 percent will potentially come from development partners, the private sector, and others; he painted a hopeful macroeconomic environment, indicating that growth will also occasion a 23.6 percent increase in per capita GDP, from approximately US$850 to US$1,050, while creating new jobs and formalizing existing ones.

a3927.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a3927.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.speech: “On the human capital front, the Plan aspires to extend life expectancy from 60 to 65 years, reduce the maternal mortality rate from 742 per 100,000 to 440 per 100,000, and reduce multidimensional poverty rate from 45 percent to 36 percent,” he said. “These and other socioeconomic achievements are expected to improve Liberia’s ranking on the SDG index by 7 places, moving from 152 out of 166 countries to 145 out of 166.”

a3927.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a3927.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.speech: Named the six pillars of AAID as Economic Transformation, Infrastructure Development, Rule of Law, Governance and Anti-Corruption, Environmental Sustainability, and Human Capital Development; said at the heart of the AAID is an innovative approach that integrates critical development priorities and cross-cutting themes to maximize the impact of interventions, including agribusiness, infrastructure, education, healthcare, and tourism, and that the AAID is underpinned by principles of inclusiveness, sustainability, justice and equality, accountability, peace and reconciliation, and local ownership.

a3927.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a3927.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.speech: “It reflects the aspirations of all Liberians, shaped by nationwide consultations with stakeholders including government, civil society, private sector actors, traditional leaders, the youth, People with Disabilities, and international partners,” he noted, adding: “These consultations reinforced the importance of a people-centered development, addressing systemic barriers and structural inequalities while prioritizing the empowerment of marginalized communities.”

a3927.speaker: Augustine K. Ngafuan, Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.name: Augustine K. Ngafuan
a3927.title: Liberian Finance and Development Planning Minister
a3927.speech: “We utilize the cause-consequence approach to ensure that interventions are strategic and impactful, focusing on measurable cross-sectoral outcomes of development drivers and Filters,” he emphasized. “Additionally, the AAID is built on a program-based approach to allow implementation of program-based budgeting, hence strengthening the linkage between the development outcomes and the national budget.”

a4022.speaker: Dr. Athar Ali, Head of Surgery unit at Aga Khan Hospital
a4022.name: Dr. Athar Ali
a4022.title: Head of Surgery unit at Aga Khan Hospital
a4022.speech: Shared that the initiative has successfully restored smiles and improved the lives of women and girls who have faced physical challenges such as mobility impairments, burn injuries, gender-based violence, and disabilities resulting from accidents ; “This program has been made possible with the expertise of specialist doctors from RWI, the U.S., Canada, and Europe, working alongside teams from Aga Khan, Muhimbili, Bugando, and Mnazimmoja hospitals in Zanzibar” ; further added that since the program’s launch in 2016, over 300 women and girls have benefited.

a4022.speaker: Dr. Andrea Pusic, plastic surgeon and leader of Reconstruction Women International (RWI) in the U.S.
a4022.name: Dr. Andrea Pusic
a4022.title: plastic surgeon and leader of Reconstruction Women International (RWI) in the U.S.
a4022.speech: Emphasized that the goal of the program is to help women and girls regain physical functionality and dignity, recognizing their role in contributing to both the economy and their families ; “This is the ninth year of our successful partnership. We’ve not only improved their physical abilities and appearance, but we’ve also been providing training to doctors, enabling them to perform these life-changing surgeries.”

a4022.speaker: Dr. Aidan Njau, specialist surgeon at Aga Khan Hospital
a4022.name: Dr. Aidan Njau
a4022.title: specialist surgeon at Aga Khan Hospital
a4022.speech: Revealed that while the program initially served only patients from Dar es Salaam, it now reaches women and girls from all over the country ; further outlined that the focus is on those with the most severe cases.

a4022.speaker: Dr. Edwin Mrema, body reconstruction specialist at Muhimbili National Hospital
a4022.name: Dr. Edwin Mrema
a4022.title: body reconstruction specialist at Muhimbili National Hospital
a4022.speech: Shared that when the program began, there were no specialized surgeons in this field in Tanzania; however, thanks to the collaboration with the government and various training programs including those at the Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences, nine surgeons have now been trained, with plans for more specialists to be trained annually.

a4179.speaker: Gen Godfrey Otunge, commander of the Multinational Security Support mission (MSS)
a4179.name: Gen Godfrey Otunge
a4179.title: commander of the Multinational Security Support mission (MSS)
a4179.speech: Said the Kenyan police officer had been injured in Artibonite, a region north of the capital ; said the officer, who has not been named, had been immediately airlifted to hospital, where he died a short while later.

a4179.speaker: Jack Ombaka, spokesman for the MSS (statement sent to Reuters)
a4179.name: Jack Ombaka
a4179.title: spokesman for the MSS (statement sent to Reuters)
a4179.speech: Said in a statement that the officer was a “fallen hero” who “was killed while fighting for the people of Haiti” ; said the officer had been shot by a gang member during a security operation in the town of Pont-Sondé ; added that the multinational force would “pursue these gangs to the last man standing.”

a4179.speaker: Kenya’s foreign ministry
a4179.name: Kenya’s foreign ministry
a4179.speech: Said it was “heartbroken by the loss” of the officer.

a4237.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4237.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4237.speech: According to OCHA, more than five million people in 16 countries of West and Central Africa have been affected by floods since the beginning of the year, with Chad, Niger and Nigeria among the worst-hit countries, accounting for close to 80% of the people affected.

a4237.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4237.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a4237.speech: Counted, last September, more than four million people affected by the catastrophic floods caused by torrential rains in 14 countries of West Africa, in a context where the hunger crisis affects nearly 55 million people in this part of Africa.

a4237.speaker: ECOWAS Regional Integrated Agricultural Information System (Agrhymet) (published note)
a4237.name: ECOWAS Regional Integrated Agricultural Information System (Agrhymet) (published note)
a4237.speech: According to a note published by Agrhymet, the rainfall recorded in the Sahelian belt and locally in the north of the Gulf of Guinea countries was 120% to 600% above the 1991-2020 averages.

a4310.speaker: Fatouma Awaleh Osman, president of the council of Djibouti, mayor of Djibouti-city and president of the National Association of Djiboutian Local Authorities (ANCLD)
a4310.name: Fatouma Awaleh Osman
a4310.title: president of the council of Djibouti, mayor of Djibouti-city and president of the National Association of Djiboutian Local Authorities (ANCLD)
a4310.speech: Presented to the representatives of the sectoral ministries and to her technical and financial partners the strategic development plan for the city of Djibouti for the period 2020-2024, and conveyed to them the importance of this strategic plan for the development of the capital; declared that thanks to the commitment and seriousness of the various commissions in charge of drafting the document, the main areas of city management had been gone over with a fine-tooth comb – social and cultural dimension, spatial and environmental occupation, economic and financial activities, all sub-domains had been diagnosed – before thanking the delegation of the European Union, whose financial support made it possible to draft the document, the AIMF for its technical support, and all the development partners contributing to the realisation of the city’s actions.

a4310.speaker: Bernard François, head of cooperation of the Delegation of the European Union, and Kutluhan Yucel, resident coordinator of the Turkish Cooperation Agency (TIKA) in Djibouti
a4310.name: Bernard François
a4310.title: head of cooperation of the Delegation of the European Union, and Kutluhan Yucel, resident coordinator of the Turkish Cooperation Agency (TIKA) in Djibouti
a4310.speech: Took the floor and each in turn placed the emphasis on the actions carried out by their different institutions in the framework of the development of the city of Djibouti, and committed themselves to supporting the local elected officials in this area.

a4310.speaker: National consultant (unnamed)
a4310.name: National consultant (unnamed)
a4310.speech: Was given the floor to present the document relating to the five-year development plan of the city of Djibouti, validated by the council of Djibouti and by all the local elected officials.

a4338.speaker: Nursery growers of Niamey
a4338.name: Nursery growers of Niamey
a4338.speech: Deplore the lack of accompaniment and support in their activity, which is nevertheless indispensable for the preservation of the environment ; are issuing an appeal to the authorities and environmental organisations for strengthened support, in order to back their efforts and guarantee the preservation of threatened plant species.

a4338.speaker: Marcel Soubega, nursery grower in Niamey with more than thirty years of experience
a4338.name: Marcel Soubega
a4338.title: nursery grower in Niamey with more than thirty years of experience
a4338.speech: Regrets the absence of support from local authorities; according to him, nursery growers play an important role in maintaining biodiversity, but their contribution remains largely ignored by decision-making bodies.

a4338.speaker: Yeni Seydou, nursery grower in Niamey
a4338.name: Yeni Seydou
a4338.title: nursery grower in Niamey
a4338.speech: Stresses that the absence of initiatives to help nursery growers acquire and conserve plants is causing certain varieties to become rare, or even to disappear entirely from the country ; proposes that the State and specialised organisations search for good foreign plant species and make them available to nursery growers for trials and experiments ; says the high cost of imports prevents willing nursery growers from introducing new varieties, thereby limiting the diversity of crops.

a4395.speaker: Trading Economics (data)
a4395.name: Trading Economics (data)
a4395.speech: According to data from Trading Economics, Mali's military spending went from $582 million in 2022 to $784.50 million in 2023.

a4395.speaker: Foundation for Studies and Research on International Development (Ferdi) (report)
a4395.name: Foundation for Studies and Research on International Development (Ferdi) (report)
a4395.speech: According to a Ferdi report, between 2010 and 2014 the military spending of Sahelian countries averaged $1.136 billion per year, half of it coming from Chad.

a4395.speaker: UNICEF
a4395.name: UNICEF
a4395.speech: According to UNICEF, over the past year the sharp increase in insecurity, violence and military operations has hampered humanitarian actors' access to conflict-affected populations.

a4492.speaker: Marc Weinstock, U.S. Embassy Charge d'Affaires in Eswatini
a4492.name: Marc Weinstock
a4492.title: U.S. Embassy Charge d'Affaires in Eswatini
a4492.speech: Emphasized the United States' continued commitment to supporting Eswatini in addressing public health challenges: "PEPFAR and the U.S. Government remain committed to supporting countries in maintaining the response we have jointly built. We look forward to continued collaboration under the United States' new Global Health Strategy that was released at UNGA last week. These vehicles that we hand over today represent resources provided by the United States."

a4492.speaker: Khanyakwezwe Mabuza, Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a4492.name: Khanyakwezwe Mabuza
a4492.title: Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Health of Eswatini
a4492.speech: Expressed gratitude on behalf of the Ministry and the Government of Eswatini, noting that the vehicles would greatly enhance the efficiency of health interventions: "This generous contribution will make a tangible difference in our ability to deliver quality services to the people of Eswatini." ; "Reliable transportation is critical for timely outreach, monitoring, and delivery of health programmes. We are thankful to the United States Government and PEPFAR for their unwavering support."

a4492.speaker: Nsindiso Tsabedze, Ministry of Health Communication Officer
a4492.name: Nsindiso Tsabedze
a4492.title: Ministry of Health Communication Officer
a4492.speech: Pointed out in an interview with this publication that the vehicles had previously been utilised by other NGOs and hence the fact that they completed their designed programs, the US saw the Ministry's need and handed over these vehicles.

a4555.speaker: Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (analysis)
a4555.name: Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) (analysis)
a4555.speech: According to IGAD, approximately 50.6 million people or 20 percent of the total population in the east Africa region are at risk of being food insecure and require food assistance by the end of 2020 ; the analysis by IGAD states that the compounding impacts of the COVID-19 global pandemic, desert locust invasion, ongoing climatic shocks, conflict and insecurity, adverse macroeconomic shocks, together with protracted food insecurity from past shocks, could lead to a food security crisis in the region.

a4555.speaker: IGAD Food Security and Nutrition Response Strategy (document)
a4555.name: IGAD Food Security and Nutrition Response Strategy (document)
a4555.speech: Calls upon member states and partners to provide technical and financial support to IGAD to implement a series of short-term interventions to deal with the unfolding crisis.

a4555.speaker: Workneh Gebeyehu, IGAD Executive Secretary
a4555.name: Workneh Gebeyehu
a4555.title: IGAD Executive Secretary
a4555.speech: “Nearly 50.6 million people are projected to be food insecure by the end of 2020 in the IGAD region. With millions of vulnerable populations at risk, IGAD has taken a stance to curb the casualties. This strategy puts in place guidelines for a coherent approach to supporting our citizens and the region. We call on Member States and partners to work together to provide political, technical and financial support to IGAD in the implementation of this comprehensive regional strategy.”

a5047.speaker: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) (statement)
a5047.name: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) (statement)
a5047.speech: Said in a statement issued Monday that its initial assessment indicated no civilians were harmed in the April 16 airstrike targeting al-Shabaab militants near Adan Yabaal district, conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia; the number of al-Shabaab militants killed has not yet been disclosed ; reiterated its commitment to working alongside Somali and international partners: "We will continue to take action to degrade al-Shabaab's ability to plan and conduct attacks that threaten the U.S. homeland, our forces, and our citizens abroad."

a5047.speaker: Somali security official (anonymous, quoted by the Anadolu news agency)
a5047.name: Somali security official (anonymous
a5047.title: quoted by the Anadolu news agency)
a5047.speech: Said militants launched a coordinated pre-dawn assault on Adan Yabaal on April 16, forcing government troops to withdraw after hours of intense combat.

a5354.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5354.name: Marco Rubio
a5354.title: US Secretary of State
a5354.speech: Paid tribute to the leadership of King Mohammed VI in promoting peace and security at the regional and international levels; in a statement issued on Monday in Washington following a telephone conversation with Moroccan Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita, he highlighted the importance of the strategic partnership between Morocco and the United States, underlining the Sovereign's key role in maintaining peace and security in the world.

a5354.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5354.name: Marco Rubio
a5354.title: US Secretary of State
a5354.speech: Expressed the United States' desire to deepen its cooperation with Morocco in order to promote common interests and resolve conflicts, particularly within the framework of the Abraham Accords.

a5354.speaker: US State Department spokesperson (statement)
a5354.name: US State Department spokesperson (statement)
a5354.speech: Specified that the discussions focused in particular on the ceasefire agreement in Gaza, the release of the hostages, as well as Morocco's role in delivering humanitarian aid to the Palestinians.

a5354.speaker: US State Department (statement)
a5354.name: US State Department (statement)
a5354.speech: Concludes that the conversation made it possible to reaffirm the importance of strengthening trade and investment between the two nations, for the benefit of both peoples.

a5441.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID Mission Director in Mozambique
a5441.name: Helen Pataki
a5441.title: USAID Mission Director in Mozambique
a5441.speech: Lauded the continuing collaboration between the United States and Mozambique to support the private sector, the results of which are illustrated by the award winners. “The U.S. government shares a vision with all our partners to promote the role of private sector-led economic growth,” Director Pataki said. ; “USAID and the broader U.S. government are committed to promoting inclusive, sustained, and resilient economic growth in developing countries including Mozambique.”

a5441.speaker: The award winners (Mozambican exporters)
a5441.name: The award winners (Mozambican exporters)
a5441.speech: The award winners, who all export agricultural products such as nuts, bananas, and tea, underscored the need to diversify the Mozambican export sector.

a5518.speaker: Niamey (Niger’s transitional authorities)
a5518.name: Niamey (Niger’s transitional authorities)
a5518.speech: According to Niamey, not only had this aid not been requested by the transitional authorities, but the funds were also said to have been allocated directly by the European ambassador to several international NGOs operating in the country.

a5518.speaker: Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5518.name: Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a5518.speech: Cites, for example, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Danish Refugee Council; the authorities denounce a “contempt for the principles of transparency and good collaboration” and announce that they have commissioned an audit to establish the “real use and destination” of the funding.

a5584.speaker: Crisis Group (report)
a5584.name: Crisis Group (report)
a5584.speech: Recommends that Somalia urgently needs to build infrastructure to withstand future extreme weather more effectively, that Mogadishu needs help with adaptation measures while funds are trickling in, and that given the country’s immense needs, the government should consider making climate resilience a central part of its efforts to engage Al-Shabaab in talks; the report draws upon more than 150 interviews with residents of southern and central Somalia, current and former Somali officials, employees of the UN and other international bodies, NGO representatives, researchers, journalists and academics.

a5584.speaker: Crisis Group research/analysis
a5584.name: Crisis Group research/analysis
a5584.speech: Recorded 127 deliveries of food and water claimed by Al-Shabaab in eleven regions between April 2021 and November 2022, and its analysis of videos posted by Al-Shabaab suggests that the deliveries were as much a propaganda exercise as a genuine attempt to ease food shortages ; research shows that Al-Shabaab’s actions during the 2020-2023 drought worsened conditions for the population; it identified at least 65 attacks on both convoys carrying food supplies and wells between October 2020 and December 2022, nearly twice the number that had occurred in the two previous years ; using satellite imagery, confirmed the construction of a reservoir, a canal and a water tower in Buulo Fulaay, and verified work in three locations where Al-Shabaab claims to have rehabilitated canals.

a5584.speaker: Data from NASA, the Climate Hazards Center at the University of California-Santa Barbara and the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED)
a5584.name: Data from NASA
a5584.title: the Climate Hazards Center at the University of California-Santa Barbara and the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED)
a5584.speech: Cited as the sources for the report’s figures on vegetation density, rainfall anomalies and conflict events involving Al-Shabaab.

a5584.speaker: Scientists
a5584.name: Scientists
a5584.speech: Say climate change made this drought 100 [times] more likely than usual.

a5584.speaker: The UN
a5584.name: The UN
a5584.speech: Described the March-April 2023 flooding of the Juba and Shabelle rivers, which displaced around 100,000 people in Somalia, as a once-in-a-century event ; according to the UN, an additional 228,237 people have been displaced since April, due to flooding, drought and conflict.

a5584.speaker: Climate experts in Somalia
a5584.name: Climate experts in Somalia
a5584.speech: Note that dry soil becomes less capable of absorbing water, limiting the recharge of groundwater and aquifers that nourish plants and roots.

a5584.speaker: UN sanctions monitors
a5584.name: UN sanctions monitors
a5584.speech: Noted in 2019 that Al-Shabaab had stopped taxing charcoal and instead started sabotaging charcoal shipments, probably in a bid to undermine Jubaland’s export earnings.

a5584.speaker: Observers
a5584.name: Observers
a5584.speech: Say militants sought to maintain the forest cover in order to shield themselves from drone attacks.

a5584.speaker: A trader from Adan Yabaal
a5584.name: A trader from Adan Yabaal
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that Al-Shabaab expected residents to maintain the diesel pumps on boreholes but forced them to pay for their livestock’s water as well.

a5584.speaker: Senior Somali politicians and aid workers
a5584.name: Senior Somali politicians and aid workers
a5584.speech: Blamed Al-Shabaab for the famine in 2011, which killed a quarter of a million people, mainly children.

a5584.speaker: One mayor
a5584.name: One mayor
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that residents were punished for refusing to use Al-Shabaab’s justice systems or pay its “taxes”.

a5584.speaker: Somali employees of an international NGO
a5584.name: Somali employees of an international NGO
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that they were able to enter villages close to Al-Shabaab-controlled territory from late 2022 onward, apparently with the group’s tacit consent.

a5584.speaker: A Somali NGO
a5584.name: A Somali NGO
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that Al-Shabaab reached out to local businesspeople and elders in 2022 to request that they help people displaced by the drought with water and cash, and that the NGO declined to assist due to donor restrictions on engagement with Al-Shabaab.

a5584.speaker: Aid workers and security officials
a5584.name: Aid workers and security officials
a5584.speech: Reported that Al-Shabaab fighters and their families in the Al-Shabaab-controlled Gedo and Bay regions looked thin and physically weak.

a5584.speaker: Male defectors
a5584.name: Male defectors
a5584.speech: Reportedly told Somali security forces that they survived on a single portion of white rice per day.

a5584.speaker: Some humanitarian workers
a5584.name: Some humanitarian workers
a5584.speech: Are hopeful that Al-Shabaab will eventually relax its restrictions on aid further.

a5584.speaker: Al-Shabaab (video released May 2023)
a5584.name: Al-Shabaab (video released May 2023)
a5584.speech: Released a video featuring the reservoir it built in Buulo Fulaay, with supposedly prominent locals saying the nearest alternative water source was 60km away ; the group also claimed responsibility for at least eighteen attacks between January and February, including several on water trucks using improvised explosive devices.

a5584.speaker: An Al-Shabaab leader
a5584.name: An Al-Shabaab leader
a5584.speech: Spoke of plans for similar reservoirs elsewhere.

a5584.speaker: Displaced people in Baidoa and Dollow
a5584.name: Displaced people in Baidoa and Dollow
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that they were afraid of being imprisoned, tortured or killed if caught leaving Al-Shabaab territory; several people told Crisis Group that they fled Al-Shabaab’s rule because they could not meet the group’s onerous tax demands, because they did not have enough food or water, or both.

a5584.speaker: Confidential UN report (September 2023)
a5584.name: Confidential UN report (September 2023)
a5584.speech: Revealed cases of extortion of cash assistance in 55 displacement camps.

a5584.speaker: Critics of fluctuating humanitarian relief
a5584.name: Critics of fluctuating humanitarian relief
a5584.speech: Argue that this pattern of aid disrupts long-term local peace efforts and draws communities toward overcrowded areas where resources are constantly running low, and have proposed redirecting a larger proportion of aid to projects that can bolster Somalia’s resilience to climate shocks.

a5584.speaker: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
a5584.name: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
a5584.speech: Signed an agreement in October with the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Somali government for a $95 million climate resilience project, which it says will benefit around 1.2 million Somalis nationwide.

a5584.speaker: Denmark
a5584.name: Denmark
a5584.speech: Has pledged $150 million to Somalia over the next five years, with approximately 40 per cent of this amount earmarked for conflict-sensitive climate adaptation projects.

a5584.speaker: Officials involved in Somali water and irrigation initiatives, such as the Deegan Bile projects in Galmudug and Hirshabelle
a5584.name: Officials involved in Somali water and irrigation initiatives
a5584.title: such as the Deegan Bile projects in Galmudug and Hirshabelle
a5584.speech: Say donors and communities have drawn many lessons from their experiences: dialogue with local communities and clear, agreed norms for managing natural resources tend to reduce conflict risks and can enhance local authorities’ legitimacy.

a5584.speaker: Some international donors
a5584.name: Some international donors
a5584.speech: Told Crisis Group that they need to see more progress on the issue of fighting corruption in Somalia.

a5584.speaker: A major GCF donor
a5584.name: A major GCF donor
a5584.speech: Noted that Somalia and other conflict-affected countries should bolster the state’s fiscal management, such as tax systems, in order to become credible loan recipients.

a5584.speaker: REACH, a humanitarian initiative (data)
a5584.name: REACH
a5584.title: a humanitarian initiative (data)
a5584.speech: Data has highlighted a steep decline in herders’ livelihoods in Xarardheere district in Mudug, which was under Al-Shabaab’s control until January 2023.

a5584.speaker: Credible sources
a5584.name: Credible sources
a5584.speech: Have indicated to Crisis Group that constituencies within Al-Shabaab may be more amenable to negotiations than its public statements suggest.

a5648.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cape Verde
a5648.name: Olavo Correia
a5648.title: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cape Verde
a5648.speech: Admitted concern about the possible closure of the American agency Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), but rejected “lamentations” and indicated that he is looking for alternatives ; said Cape Verde has not yet been officially notified about the closure of the agency, but stressed that according to “data he has, there is a very strong probability of that happening” ; said the closure of the agency is a decision that “harms Africa and harms Cape Verde” ; “We will only take a formal position on this matter when the Government is notified,” but as Minister of Finance he looks at the situation “with some concern,” because it is a project for which Cape Verde had great expectations in terms of amounts and sectors ; “Hearing the information that it may be closed is something that worries us” ; “As political managers, what we have to do is: we cannot have an attitude of lamentation. So, if it is a fact, we have to accept it as such when we come to be informed and look for other partnerships. That is our role. But of course I would not have liked to receive that communication” ; said he was prepared for that possibility and stressed that the Cape Verdean Government “is already looking for alternatives for this eventual closure of the MCC package.”

a5648.speaker: Internal memorandum cited by the France-Presse news agency
a5648.name: Internal memorandum cited by the France-Presse news agency
a5648.speech: States that the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by billionaire Elon Musk, will impose “significant reductions” in the number of staff and programmes of the agency.

a5648.speaker: Politico (US news site)
a5648.name: Politico (US news site)
a5648.speech: Adds that the agency is expected to lay off its 320 employees and end grants to about 40 developing countries where it has projects.

a5648.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Cape Verde (data)
a5648.name: Ministry of Finance of Cape Verde (data)
a5648.speech: According to its data, the country benefited from its first MCC compact in July 2005, when the Government and the American agency signed a five-year agreement worth 110 million dollars (97 million euros) to help increase economic growth and reduce poverty through investments in infrastructure, watershed management, support for agriculture and private sector development; the second package was approved in 2012 and the archipelago benefited from 66.2 million dollars (58 million euros) to reduce poverty through economic growth.

a5709.speaker: Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of the Russian Security Council
a5709.name: Dmitry Medvedev
a5709.title: Deputy Chairman of the Russian Security Council
a5709.speech: "From now on, the country which is on the verge of disappearing will have to use its national wealth to pay for its military supplies," declared the deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council ; "Trump has finally pressured the Kyiv regime into financing American aid with its mineral resources. From now on the country, in the process of disappearing, will have to use its national wealth to finance its military supplies," he wrote on Telegram.

a5709.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5709.name: Donald Trump
a5709.title: US President
a5709.speech: Earlier, Trump had confirmed that Washington and Kyiv had concluded an agreement on US access to Ukraine's mineral resources.

a5724.speaker: Falola Djogbenou Venise, president of WROP BENIN
a5724.name: Falola Djogbenou Venise
a5724.title: president of WROP BENIN
a5724.speech: Said the project "Developing the advocacy efforts of women of the North on security matters" was carried out in three northern departments - Alibori, Donga and Atacora - and aims to identify the advocacy issues of local women on questions linked to security, in the hope that national leaders and decision-makers will listen and take measures alongside the beneficiary communities to ease these women's hardships. ; "It was a matter of going out to meet these women, listening to them and taking in everything they had in the way of difficulties linked to security. And when we speak of security, it is security in all its senses: food security, physical security, moral security... these were conversations that took place in local languages. In each department or in each commune, the women expressed themselves in their language, and this together with their women parliamentarians who were on tour with us. At the end of this tour, we organised an activity in Parakou... Now, together with the 29 women parliamentarians and the 48 women who had been selected at the level of each commune, we drew up an action plan and, in relation to that, the women also identified three major axes. It is these axes, this action plan, that we want today to present back to the whole Beninese nation, and this still together with the women parliamentarians."

a5724.speaker: Falola Djogbenou Venise, president of WROP BENIN
a5724.name: Falola Djogbenou Venise
a5724.title: president of WROP BENIN
a5724.speech: Said that the women parliamentarians, after the various activities, made commitments towards the local women, which they will present at the workshop - commitments on specific advocacy themes as well as personal ones: helping a maternity ward, advocating that the Ministry of Health send staff or ask staff to review their behaviour, equipping a women's cooperative with a motor pump or an irrigation system.

a5724.speaker: Falola Djogbenou Venise, president of WROP BENIN
a5724.name: Falola Djogbenou Venise
a5724.title: president of WROP BENIN
a5724.speech: "There are also axes that must be presented to the technical and financial partners, to the institutions of the Republic, to the ministries. Each one will come and say what it can do in all that the women have listed as needs and that are found in this action plan. So this is not a piece of work that we went and did in the field only to put the results away in a cupboard. With USAID, which is supporting us, we are going to present these results to everyone, because it is Beninese women who for the first time have expressed their needs out loud to their women parliamentarians."

a5724.speaker: Falola Djogbenou Venise, president of WROP BENIN
a5724.name: Falola Djogbenou Venise
a5724.title: president of WROP BENIN
a5724.speech: Thanked USAID and the Embassy of the United States in Benin, which continue to provide their unfailing support to the WROP BENIN platform; told partners who are still hesitating that WROP BENIN is a platform that works for the defence of women's rights, their empowerment and their representation in all decision-making bodies.

a5802.speaker: José Tonato, Minister of Living Environment and Infrastructure, in charge of Sustainable Development (Benin)
a5802.name: José Tonato
a5802.title: Minister of Living Environment and Infrastructure, in charge of Sustainable Development (Benin)
a5802.speech: According to him, the ambition by 2040 is for Benin's forest areas to be better managed for their multiple functions.

a5802.speaker: Representative of Sweden (project financial partner)
a5802.name: Representative of Sweden (project financial partner)
a5802.speech: “We hope that this project will be implemented successfully for the well-being of the communities.”

a5802.speaker: Ange Obama, FAO Resident Representative
a5802.name: Ange Obama
a5802.title: FAO Resident Representative
a5802.speech: For him, wetland forests constitute an important source of fuel and food but are extremely affected by degradation; implementing specific actions under the project 'Global forest transformation for people and climate: Focus on West Africa' will be beneficial for communities and will contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

a5881.speaker: GIZ (press statement)
a5881.name: GIZ (press statement)
a5881.speech: In a press statement released on Wednesday, November 13, 2024, said the newly inaugurated sports arena at the Crop Training Center includes football, volleyball, and netball pitches for co-curricular activities; that the four curricula for certificate courses and accompanying institutional policy documents were developed with support from GIZ and GOPA on behalf of the German Development Cooperation; that the course topics were identified based on a labour market and organizational capacity assessment; that the certificate courses have already met huge interest with enrolment rates for self-sponsored students rising rapidly; and that support was provided by the project "Improved Living Conditions and Psychosocial Support in the Context of Forced Displacement (ILIPS)" implemented by GIZ and its partner GOPA on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

a5991.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5991.name: Marco Rubio
a5991.title: US Secretary of State
a5991.speech: In March, said the Trump administration had cancelled more than 80 percent of all the USAID programmes.

a5991.speaker: Oxfam International, global advocacy group
a5991.name: Oxfam International
a5991.title: global advocacy group
a5991.speech: Saying the cuts to development aid were the largest since 1960.

a5991.speaker: United Nations
a5991.name: United Nations
a5991.speech: Puts the growing gap in annual development finance at $4 trillion.

a5991.speaker: Conference organisers (UN Conference on Financing Development)
a5991.name: Conference organisers (UN Conference on Financing Development)
a5991.speech: Have said the key focus of the talks is restructuring finance for the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted at the last meeting in 2015 and expected to be met by 2030.

a5991.speaker: Chola Milambo, Zambia’s permanent representative to the UN
a5991.name: Chola Milambo
a5991.title: Zambia’s permanent representative to the UN
a5991.speech: Said the document shows that the world can tackle the financial challenges in the way of achieving the development goals, “and that multilateralism can still work”.

a5991.speaker: Oxfam
a5991.name: Oxfam
a5991.speech: Has condemned the document for lacking ambition and said “the interests of a very wealthy are put over those of everyone else”.

a6034.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU High Representative/Vice President, and Heiko Josef Maas, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Germany (joint op-ed)
a6034.name: Josep Borrell
a6034.title: EU High Representative/Vice President, and Heiko Josef Maas, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Germany (joint op-ed)
a6034.speech: "We offered the new authorities our full support" ; argued that to provide a lifeline to the on-going transition and accompany Sudan's own efforts, increased international political and financial assistance remains essential, and that the moment to do so is now to avoid any backsliding in the transition ; announced that on 25 June the United Nations, the European Union, Germany and Sudan will convene an international conference to send a strong message to the Sudanese people: "the international community continues to stand behind your democratic transition!" ; said around 50 countries and international organisations are offering Sudan a partnership to support the country up to the elections in 2022, that they plan to raise enough funds to kick-start a social protection programme by the World Bank and the Sudanese Government, and that they will support the International Monetary Fund in opening up Sudan's road towards debt relief ; "your sacrifices were not in vain. The 'new Sudan' is here to stay. We won't let you fall."

a6034.speaker: First civilian Government of Sudan (Transitional Government)
a6034.name: First civilian Government of Sudan (Transitional Government)
a6034.speech: Pledged to meet the peoples' aspirations for "freedom, peace and justice."

a6034.speaker: United Nations Security Council
a6034.name: United Nations Security Council
a6034.speech: Agreed to mandate a new political UN mission to assist Sudan on its road to peace and democracy.

a6034.speaker: Sudanese protesters
a6034.name: Sudanese protesters
a6034.speech: "Just fall, that's all" was one of the slogans that protesters chanted on the streets of Khartoum to oust the old regime.

a6049.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a6049.name: Elon Musk
a6049.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a6049.speech: Described sweeping government cuts as “common sense” measures that are “not draconian or radical” ; “The people voted for major government reform and that's what the people are going to get. That's what democracy is all about” ; “I fully expect to be scrutinised. It's not like I think I can get away with something” ; described federal workers as an “unelected, fourth, unconstitutional branch of government” that he said has “more power than any elected representative” ; “It's not optional for us to reduce the federal expenses. It's essential. It's essential for America to remain solvent as a country.”

a6049.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a6049.name: Elon Musk
a6049.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge)
a6049.speech: Asked about a recent false claim that the US government was sending millions of dollars worth of condoms to Gaza, replied: “Some of the things that I say will be incorrect and should be corrected.”

a6049.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6049.name: Donald Trump
a6049.title: US President
a6049.speech: “We found fraud and abuse,” Trump said of Musk's work on Tuesday, without providing evidence; he estimated more than US$1 trillion in wasteful spending would be discovered although gave no further details.

a6049.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6049.name: Donald Trump
a6049.title: US President
a6049.speech: “I hope that the court system is going to allow us to do what we have to do,” referring to recent judgments that have temporarily halted his efforts to shrink government, including through an employee buyout programme.

a6049.speaker: Chuck Schumer, Senate Minority Leader
a6049.name: Chuck Schumer
a6049.title: Senate Minority Leader
a6049.speech: “An unelected shadow government is conducting a hostile takeover of the federal government” ; said Democrats would work to block Musk's efforts by introducing specific language into spending bills.

a6049.speaker: Democrats
a6049.name: Democrats
a6049.speech: Have criticised the agency (Doge) and accused it of a lack of transparency ; have accused Musk of personally benefitting from some of the changes the Trump administration is trying to push through.

a6405.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a6405.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a6405.title: President of Zambia
a6405.speech: Says Zambia was shifting its focus from metal exports to agriculture, with an ambitious goal of exporting US$1 billion worth of beef annually in the coming years; said the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Angola had been identified as the country's initial target markets under this export diversification.

a6453.speaker: Arab citizens in Israel (protesters in Lod)
a6453.name: Arab citizens in Israel (protesters in Lod)
a6453.speech: Warn that all Palestinians in Gaza are going hungry, with children the most affected, because of the months-long Israeli blockade, which has cut off the supply of infant formula and other vital supplies ; appeal to the Israeli government to end the hunger by allowing humanitarian aid into the Gaza Strip ; accuse the government of using hunger as a weapon of war ; recall that some journalists died during the attacks carried out by Israeli forces.

a6465.speaker: Glenda Gray, president of the Medical Research Council (MRC)
a6465.name: Glenda Gray
a6465.title: president of the Medical Research Council (MRC)
a6465.speech: Said molecules that can elicit an immune response against the virus have already been identified for development into vaccine contenders ; said that to deliver the chosen molecules in the most effective way, a wide variety of options are being considered, including mRNA technology used in some Covid-19 shots, as well as protein and nano-particle-based options, and other platforms with new ingredients that may help create a stronger immune response in people receiving the vaccine.

a6465.speaker: John Nkengasong, head of PEPFAR
a6465.name: John Nkengasong
a6465.title: head of PEPFAR
a6465.speech: Said earlier this year that PEPFAR, initiated in 2003 by then president George W. Bush, has saved an estimated 25 million lives and allowed 5.5 million children to be born free of HIV.

a6589.speaker: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement signed by its President, Ernest Amoabeng Ortsin)
a6589.name: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement signed by its President
a6589.title: Ernest Amoabeng Ortsin)
a6589.speech: Welcomed President John Dramani Mahama's renewed commitment to addressing the funding gap created by the USAID 90-day funding freeze, describing the President's pledge, reiterated during his 2025 State of the Nation Address, as "reassuring and therapeutic" for persons living with HIV in Ghana ; noted that this was the third time in two weeks that President Mahama had assured the nation of his government's commitment to mitigating the impact of the funding shortfall, which threatened the country's health sector, particularly HIV and AIDS programmes.

a6589.speaker: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.name: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.speech: Raised concerns over a potential stockout of life-saving antiretroviral (ARV) medications if the government was forced to fully finance ARV procurement, a fear further exacerbated by previous delays in clearing donated ARVs from the country's ports, a situation that left many persons living with HIV anxious about their treatment ; emphasized that more needs to be done to ensure all persons living with HIV receive proper care and life-saving medication.

a6589.speaker: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.name: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.speech: Is urging the government to operationalise the National HIV and AIDS Fund (NHAF) to ensure sustainable domestic financing for the fight against HIV and AIDS: "GHANET believes that reviving the NHAF will help complement international funding, such as support from the Global Fund, and ensure continuous access to ARVs and other essential HIV services." ; lamented that the lack of funding had crippled awareness campaigns that previously targeted schools, communities, religious institutions and public spaces, resulting in a new generation of young Ghanaians with little to no knowledge of HIV and AIDS, contributing to the country recording 17,700 new infections and 12,500 AIDS-related deaths in 2023.

a6589.speaker: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.name: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.speech: As a medium-term solution, is advocating for local production of ARVs and other essential HIV-related commodities such as condoms, lubricants and test kits, noting that the country had had the capacity to manufacture ARVs since 2005 and that leveraging that existing infrastructure could ensure a stable domestic supply while creating an opportunity to export ARVs to other West African countries.

a6589.speaker: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.name: Ghana HIV and AIDS Network (GHANET) (statement)
a6589.speech: Has called on the Ministers of Finance and Health to ensure that President Mahama's commitment is reflected in the 2025 budget, and further urged the government to align with the Abuja Declaration (2001), which requires African nations to allocate at least 15 per cent of their annual budgets to the health sector.

a6589.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana (2025 State of the Nation Address)
a6589.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6589.title: President of Ghana (2025 State of the Nation Address)
a6589.speech: Reiterated his renewed commitment to addressing the funding gap created by the USAID 90-day funding freeze and assured the nation of his government's commitment to mitigating the impact of the funding shortfall.

a6589.speaker: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC) (data)
a6589.name: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC) (data)
a6589.speech: According to data from the Ghana AIDS Commission, as of December 2023 only 151,000 persons living with HIV were receiving treatment — less than half of the estimated 334,000 people living with HIV in the country.

a7294.speaker: Bounia Yahaya, president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.name: Bounia Yahaya
a7294.title: president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.speech: Stressed that the government of Niger has been engaged since 2017, with the financial and technical support of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) of the United States, in a process of reform of the fertilizer sector in Niger, carried out through the Fertilizer Sector Reform Support Project (PARSEN), financed by the Millennium Challenge Account Niger (MCA-Niger) and implemented by the IFDC. This reform, he said, was initiated by the government following a diagnostic of the sector and after several studies that revealed numerous shortcomings holding back the performance of Nigerien agriculture.

a7294.speaker: Bounia Yahaya, president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.name: Bounia Yahaya
a7294.title: president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.speech: “One may cite, among others: the low productivity of agriculture and the poverty of the soils; the low consumption of fertilizer in Niger per hectare of land, which is on the order of 3 kg/ha against 12 kg/ha in the sub-region. Also, the statistics on CAIMA's imports showed Niger's fertilizer supply at less than 24,277 t in 2017, 23,353 t in 2018, and 16,321 t in 2019 (Ministry of Finance figures), whereas the needs expressed by the producers themselves range between 100,000 t and 200,000 t per year,” he explained.

a7294.speaker: Bounia Yahaya, president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.name: Bounia Yahaya
a7294.title: president of the Fertilizer Market Observatory of Niger (OMEN)
a7294.speech: According to him the reform aims on the one hand to improve the availability and accessibility for producers of quality fertilizer at affordable prices through a supply and distribution ensured by the private sector, and on the other hand to improve the yield of agricultural production through a greater use of fertilizer. The implementation of the reform plan has seen appreciable progress, he continued, including the establishment of the reform's organs and the drafting and putting in place of regulatory and legal texts. “One of the achievements of the reform is the implementation of the targeted subsidy programme under the supervision of the reform's organs with the assistance of PARSEN. This made it possible to demonstrate successfully the feasibility in Niger of a targeted subsidy operation using purchase vouchers. This subsidy method allows not only the targeting of beneficiaries, but also accountability, transparency, traceability and close monitoring of operations.”

a7294.speaker: Dr Soumaila Abdourahamane, president of the Nigerien Association of Fertilizer Importers and Distributors (ANIDE)
a7294.name: Dr Soumaila Abdourahamane
a7294.title: president of the Nigerien Association of Fertilizer Importers and Distributors (ANIDE)
a7294.speech: Recalled that since 2019 the association counts among its ranks more than 200 members and no fewer than 400 wholesale and retail fertilizer distributors and importers. “We cover practically the whole country and in all the zones of intensive agricultural production we have sales points. Today, the actors have a good command of their marketing approach, they have a better knowledge of fertilizer in order to improve agricultural production significantly. These are very positive effects of the reform which have allowed the actors to professionalize,” he concluded.

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: Used the Ministry of Information regular press briefing on Thursday, February 13, 2025 to explain the LACC programs and activities, which she said include the mandate to educate the public about corruption, the ills about corruption, and the benefits that come with eradicating corruption in Liberia.

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: “At LACC we have four departments. One of the departments is the Department of Investigation and Monitoring. The next is the Department of Prosecution. The other is the Department of Education and Prevention; and the last is the Department of Administration.” ; “Last year, in total we investigated and completed 24 cases. We have done our Annual Report. We have published it on our website in keeping with the law. We have also served our principals, the Legislative and Executive Branches of Government.” ; “In 2024 we investigated the Ministry of Finance and completed that case. We investigated the Wash Commission, NOCAL, the Ministry of State payroll padding case, in addition to other cases that were brought in either by whistleblowers or the ones we took from the media. I will ask the media to work with us to share the list of those cases that we have concluded.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: On why the LACC does not speak about ongoing investigations: “Most of the times, the question that I get is why you don’t speak on the investigation that you conducted. Again, I would like to use this opportunity to say to the public that it makes sense to carry the public along with the LACC as we do our investigation. But my hands are tied because the Act establishing the LACC as amended in 2022 prohibits me in any form and manner to make these revelations especially when I am investigating. I will encourage us to take a copy of the LACC Act of 2022, it’s on our website, and just go through it to understand what we can do and what we cannot do. We didn’t make the law.” ; said the legislature in its wisdom decided that the LACC will be prohibited from speaking on investigations simply because under Liberian laws one is presumed innocent until tried by a competent court of jurisdiction ; “Additionally, we are a security institution. If we come to the public and start saying step by step what we are doing in our investigation, who our intel are, it places the person who is being investigated on the alert because they will know exactly what to do, and the entire process could be compromised. Criminals are very smart.” ; “The LACC is hiding nothing from the public. We will just ask the public to please work with us. We will not release investigative information when we are investigating. The law says we will only release investigative information until we obtain an indictment from the court and serve the indictment on the person, then we can come to the public and say we have arrested Mr. John Brown for this crime and then we will disclose the report on the entire investigation.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: Said the LACC has six cases that are currently being investigated: the NOCAL case, the National Road Fund case, the CBL case, the LTA case and the LRRRC case which “we are trying our best to be able to conclude by the end of this first quarter” ; said the LTA and the LRRRC cases, because they started last year, “we are trying to conclude by the end of February. But I know the public is hungry for information. The public also is concerned because investigation takes time. But it is not something that we are doing intentionally.” ; “Take for example, we are investigating John Doe. We bring him, and he comes with his lawyers. He is read his rights. Sometimes the lawyers will ask us for two weeks for his client to compile documents to come back. Sometimes the new head of the institution we are investigating will ask for time to put the documents together. Sometimes our people will have to physically leave Monrovia and move our entire investigative team to Gbarpolu for example, go there, do interviews, do physical verification, come back and compile the report. This is not intended to delay, but we just to be sure.” ; said the LACC does not want the situation where it goes to court “and because we did not do our homework properly, the cause will go against the government of Liberia which is not a good reflection of our efforts to fight corruption” ; “We want to assure the public that we are working closely with the court. In the next few weeks, we will be coming up with indictments in these cases that we have concluded.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: On prosecutions: “For prosecution, last year we prosecuted six cases. When we say prosecution, it does not only mean when we go to court and present evidence and the judgment is given in the case. From the day we get an indictment, up to the day we get judgment or verdict, it is prosecution. Last year, we got an indictment in six cases.” ; said one is the LISGIS case, the Red Cross case, Planned Parenthood case, Lower Bank, Margibi County, and the Financial Intelligence Agency ; “Out of these six cases, we went to four trials in three. The LACC one of the case, which is the Planned Parenthood case. In the Red Cross case we had a hung verdict, meaning we can put our pieces of evidence together, go back and retry the case.” ; “The Margibi County, I am sure we have all been following this. Due to the overcrowdedness of the docket of Criminal Court ‘C’, as well as the jurisdiction of the case, we decided to try the case. We started from Margibi but because the people who were being prosecuted lived in Margibi County, the jurors lived in Margibi County, we filed a motion before the judge for us to move the case to another county. The judge decided to move the case to Gbarnga, Bong County. We went to trial. We did everything humanly possible. We presented all the evidence to the jurors. The jurors in their frame of mind decided that the people cannot be held guilty.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: Reported that the Margibi case is a case where USAID gave money to the Republic of Liberia to be used for the Margibi County hospital: “That recording was all around here. People were sitting and talking and planning on how to divide money. You as a citizen, you are performing your duty as a juror, you in your right frame of mind decided that those people were not guilty. These are the issues we have. But we are not deterred. We will continue to go court. We will continue to provide awareness. We will continue to work with civil society organizations to do this awareness, we will continue to work with the Judiciary to keep our jurors aware on the repercussions of their actions.” ; said these are some of the things that frustrate the LACC’s efforts, warning that the fight against corruption is not just for the LACC but “It is for all of us” ; “We do our part, we compile the report, we compile the pieces of evidence, we get lawyers, we go to court, we present our case and we expect you put on a rational mind. You need to understand what is obtaining.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: On 2025 targets, education, prevention and decentralization: “For 2025 we have set targets. For investigations we have decided that we will do four cases every quarter. However, when we have a whistleblower who walks in and presents cases to us, we will take those cases. For prosecution, we decided that we will work with the court to take on at least one case every quarter. So, for this year, we intend to try four cases and see them to a logical conclusion.” ; “Now this brings us to the education and prevention aspect of our activities... The next step we are going to take at the LACC is to begin to do risks assessments with selected ministries. We will start off the pilot phase to be able to move into ministries and agencies, especially high-profile ministries and agencies to be able to identify what the processes and procedures are, and identify lapses, to be able to make recommendations to them.” ; “We are also going to take our anti-corruption efforts outside of Monrovia, meaning, decentralization is our focus. We are trying to identify Service Centers in rural areas to establish offices and hire staff that will sit there to collect information regarding corruption, and also present service to the public in the counties.” ; “Currently we have a couple of projects running with the UNDP for awareness. Last year we went to Bomi, Grand Bassa, Bong and Nimba Counties doing awareness programs. We have started engagement with the Ministry of Education to include anticorruption, specifically integrity courses in our curriculum. Once that is concluded we will do a formal launch for the public.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: On assets declaration: disclosed her institution’s role in bringing to the President’s attention the need to clamp down on errant public officials who refused to declare their assets in line with the constitution: “Since December 2023, the LACC started awareness around assets declaration. We started with the exiting officials of the former government... For that exercise we had over 250 exiting officials that came in. Then in January we started the exercise for this government or incoming government officials.” ; “The president and the vice president came in February, they started the process, and they declared their assets... In May of 2024, we specifically issued a regulation for 2024, setting June 31 as the deadline for asset declaration for all officials of government who were appointed, elected. That exercise concluded on June 31 and we came right here at MICAT and provided information. We extended that exercise up to August, then we published our listing.” ; “I went on radio shows, I even took my assets declaration team from our placed them in selected Ministries and agencies. Our people sat there, and people did not declare. I pulled my people out and took them back to my office. Then we did our recommendation to the president. On November 27, 2024, the president issued a directive to all public officials who had not declared their assets to do so within ten days. The ten days elapsed in December. Even after the president issued that directive, he did not act immediately on the recommendation because he still wanted to give public officials chance to declare.” ; “Yesterday, the president took action to suspend all public officials who had not declared their assets... I’ve been getting a lot of calls. People are telling me that we have published inaccurate listing. The listing that was published yesterday, we have placed it on our website, our Facebook page, and we published the listing in FrontPage Africa newspaper, The Inquirer. There are other listings that are floating around social media... We have amended our listing, and we stand by our listing.” ; “The primary purpose of the asset declaration exercise is to ensure that public officials comply with the national code of conduct and the LACC regulations regarding the declaration of their assets and liability. This exercise is crucial in preventing, detecting illicit enrichment, conflict of interest, and other forms of corruption.”

a7419.speaker: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe, LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.name: Cllr. Alexandra K. Zoe
a7419.title: LACC Executive Chairperson
a7419.speech: On the statistics of asset declaration: “For 2024, the LACC identified 1,986 public officials in the three branches of government who are required to declare their assets, income and liability. This number does not represent the national baseline of Liberia... To identify the national baseline, we have begun to write institutions to give us a listing of their staff, along with the positions.” ; “Out of this number, 1370 public officials were compliant, which means a 69% compliance rate. Conversely, 616 public officials from the three branches of government combined did not declare, which represents 31% of non-compliant.” ; “For the legislative branch, we identified a total of 73 elected representatives, out of which only 38 representatives were compliant... while 36 were non-compliant. We identified 56 administrative staff who are required to declare. Out of that number, only two staff were compliant.” ; “In the House of Senate, we identified 30 elected senators; only 14 senators were compliant... while 16 were non-compliant. In the Senate, we identified 44 administrative staff, only one was compliant.” ; “For the Executive branch, we identified 1,333 officials who were appointed and are required to declare their assets. Out of that number, 881 officials fully complied with the declaration, while 454 were non-compliant. We also received 110 assets declaration from non-appointed officials, thus bringing the total number of compliant in the executive branch to 991...” ; “In the judiciary branch, we identified 338 persons to declare their assets. Out of that number, all 338 declared their assets.” ; “This compliant rate indicates progress, but it also highlights areas for further action. As we move ahead, the LACC extends appreciation to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai for taking the decisive action to enforce our recommendation by suspending officials who have failed to declare their assets. This bold step reenforces the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability and the rule of law. We urge all public officials who have not declared to kindly proceed to the LACC. This is your legal obligation. We call on the citizens to please support us in this effort.”
